section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an emergency vehicle is approaching with flashing lights and/or siren, what should you do?
options: a:Make every reasonable effort to give the emergency vehicle a clear path, such as pulling to the side and stopping.,b:Speed up to get out of its way without pulling over.,c:Stop in the travel lane and block passage.,d:Continue as normal because they will find another route.
note: Yield to emergency vehicles by pulling to the side and stopping if necessary to provide a clear path for them to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Many crashes are caused by which of the following?
options: a:Driving too fast for the conditions,b:Drivers consistently checking their mirrors,c:Drivers yielding the right-of-way
note: Traveling at speeds too high for the conditions reduces reaction time and increases crash likelihood; always adjust speed to conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you stop your vehicle?
options: a:At stop signs, red lights, or when ordered by a traffic officer.,b:Only if another car is waiting at the intersection.,c:Only during rush hour.,d:If a pedestrian is nearby even without a crosswalk.
note: You are required to stop at intersections with stop signs, at red lights, and whenever a traffic officer directs you to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see a 'Merging traffic' sign on a multilane road, what should you do?
options: a:Make room for entering vehicles by changing lanes when safe.,b:Always stay at your current speed regardless of traffic.,c:Honk to warn merging drivers.,d:Stop immediately to let them in.
note: On multilane roads, move over when safe to allow entering traffic to merge smoothly and avoid creating a bottleneck.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How does alcohol affect driving performance?
options: a:It slows reflexes and reaction time.,b:It improves focus and alertness.,c:It wakes you up and sharpens judgment.,d:It has no effect if you feel sober.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that slows brain activity and impairs the skills needed for safe driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you approach an uncontrolled intersection?
options: a:Yield to vehicles approaching from your right, slow down, cover the brake, and look in all directions,b:Maintain speed and proceed,c:Assume you have the right-of-way and go first
note: At intersections with no signs or signals, yield to the vehicle on your right and be prepared to stop to avoid collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?
options: a:Proceed with caution.,b:Merging traffic.,c:Pedestrian crossing.
note: A flashing yellow light means you should slow down and proceed with caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How does increasing your speed affect your field of vision?
options: a:It decreases your field of vision making hazards harder to detect.,b:It increases your field of vision.,c:It makes it easier to see cross traffic.,d:It does not affect vision at all.
note: As speed increases, your usable field of vision narrows, so you must be extra alert to hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which steps help you drive more safely at night?
options: a:Increase following distance, avoid driving tired, and keep headlights working.,b:Use only your parking lights.,c:Drive faster to reduce exposure time.,d:Use high beams all the time.
note: Night driving reduces visibility; increase following distance, avoid driving when tired, and ensure headlights are functional.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which traffic signal gives you the right-of-way to turn left without yielding to oncoming traffic?
options: a:A green arrow pointing left.,b:A solid green light.,c:A flashing yellow light.,d:A steady red light.
note: A steady green arrow indicates you may proceed in the direction of the arrow with oncoming traffic stopped for the turning movement.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Who must yield when a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing where there is no traffic light?
options: a:Whoever started moving last.,b:The driver must yield to the pedestrian.,c:The pedestrian must yield to the turning vehicle.,d:The driver only if the pedestrian is in a marked crosswalk.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing at intersections without traffic signals; pedestrians have the right-of-way in these situations.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on a multilane highway, what must you ensure before moving into the passing lane?
options: a:The passing lane is clear and you have signaled your intention.,b:You can pass only on the right.,c:There is no one in the opposite lane.,d:Your passenger opens the door to signal intent.
note: Before passing, confirm the lane is clear and signal to notify other drivers of your lane change.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an unmarked T intersection, who must yield?
options: a:Traffic on the road that ends at the T must yield to through traffic.,b:All vehicles must stop and the first to stop has right-of-way.,c:Drivers on the right always have the right-of-way.,d:The larger vehicle always yields.
note: At an unmarked T, vehicles on the road that ends must yield to traffic on the through road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A Reduced speed 35 mph sign means:
options: a:The new 35 mph speed limit begins at the sign.,b:The reduced speed starts at the next sign only.,c:You have ample time to slow down after the sign.,d:The change is optional until enforced by a cop.
note: A posted reduced speed sign indicates that the new speed limit takes effect at the sign itself.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning or changing lanes, what must you always do?
options: a:Signal your intentions in advance, even if no traffic is visible.,b:Signal only when other vehicles are present.,c:Signal only in daylight.,d:Signal only if traveling at high speed.
note: Signaling before lane changes or turns is required by law and is a good safety habit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an intersection is blocked by traffic ahead, what should you do?
options: a:Stay out of the intersection until you can fully clear it.,b:Get as close as possible to the car ahead and wait.,c:Enter slowly and inch through the blockage.,d:Use the shoulder to get around the queued vehicles.
note: Do not enter an intersection unless you can fully clear it; blocking intersections impedes traffic flow and is unsafe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Being awake for 18 hours impairs driving similarly to having what BAC?
options: a:About 0.05 percent, similar to moderate intoxication.,b:0.00 percent — no impairment.,c:0.20 percent — extreme impairment.,d:No BAC equivalent exists.
note: Fatigue impairs driving akin to alcohol; being awake 18 hours roughly equals a BAC of 0.05% impairment.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you meet a car with high, blinding headlights, what is the best action?
options: a:Look toward the right edge of the road until the other car passes.,b:Flash your headlights to warn the other driver.,c:Use your high beams until they dim theirs.,d:Speed up to pass quickly.
note: If an oncoming vehicle has its high beams on, avert your eyes toward the right side of the road so you are not blinded.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you drive below the posted speed limit?
options: a:Whenever conditions such as wet roads, poor visibility, or anything else make driving unsafe.,b:Only when you see a police car.,c:Only when entering a busy highway.
note: You must reduce speed below the posted limit when conditions (weather, visibility, road surface) make the posted speed unsafe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When the center line is a solid yellow next to a broken yellow on your side, when may you pass?
options: a:Only in emergencies.,b:Only if you are on an expressway.,c:You may pass if the broken line is next to your lane and traffic is clear.
note: If the broken yellow line is next to your lane, you may cross it to pass when there is no oncoming traffic and it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a red-and-white triangular sign at an intersection indicate?
options: a:Yield—slow and give the right-of-way to traffic or pedestrians in the intersection,b:Always come to a full stop,c:Slow down only if an emergency vehicle is approaching
note: A triangular red-and-white sign means yield: reduce speed and be prepared to stop to let others proceed first.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How can you avoid having to make emergency stops in traffic?
options: a:Honk your horn frequently so others notice you.,b:Look ahead and maintain a safe following distance and scan for hazards.,c:Drive in the right lane only.,d:Follow the vehicle ahead very closely to anticipate stops.
note: Maintaining a safe following distance and scanning ahead allows you to react smoothly and avoid abrupt emergency stops.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If convicted of DUII for the first time, how long will your driving privileges be suspended?
options: a:One year.,b:Six months.,c:Three months.,d:Indefinitely.
note: A first DUII conviction results in a one-year license suspension under Oregon law.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct way to reduce speed when using a freeway exit ramp?
options: a:Slow down once you have moved into the exit ramp,b:Begin heavy braking on the main roadway before entering the exit lane,c:Keep your speed constant while on the ramp
note: Do not decelerate sharply on the freeway; move into the exit lane and then brake to slow to ramp speed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you approach an accident scene, how should you behave if you are not involved?
options: a:Do not stop unless you are involved or emergency help has not yet arrived; keep moving and watch for people near the road,b:Always stop to view the scene,c:Park nearby and take photos
note: Do not block emergency responders or create additional hazards; only stop if you are directly involved or help is needed before responders arrive.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does an End school zone sign indicate?
options: a:The reduced school zone speed limit is ending.,b:The school zone speed limit is starting.,c:Children are especially likely to appear here.,d:You must always stop for pedestrians now.
note: An End school zone sign marks the conclusion of the reduced speed school zone and that the special limit no longer applies.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a light rail intersection, what must you always do?
options: a:Look both ways before crossing tracks and obey all traffic signals.,b:Share the road with pedestrians and bicyclists only.,c:Ignore the crossing gates if no train is visible.,d:Follow the vehicle directly in front of you across the tracks.
note: At streetcar or light rail crossings always look both ways before turning across tracks and obey all signs and traffic signals; never drive around lowered gates.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you check your blind spot before changing lanes?
options: a:Quickly glance over your shoulder toward the lane you want to enter,b:Only look at the left side mirror,c:Only check the rearview mirror
note: After checking mirrors, glance over your shoulder to confirm no vehicle is in your blind spot before moving lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: As a pedestrian, what is the safe practice regarding entering a street or crosswalk?
options: a:Do not enter if vehicles are approaching and may not be able to stop.,b:Always insist on right-of-way over vehicles in crosswalks.,c:Enter anytime; drivers must always stop.,d:Run across quickly regardless of traffic.
note: Pedestrians should not step into a roadway when approaching vehicles may not have time to stop, even if the crosswalk legally gives pedestrians the right-of-way.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When driving in traffic, what is the safest speed choice?
options: a:Drive with the flow of traffic within the posted limit,b:Drive faster than the flow to get through quickly,c:Drive slower than the flow at all times
note: Crashes often happen when drivers go much faster or slower than surrounding traffic. Travel with the flow while obeying limits and adjusting for conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which is not a factor in stopping distance?
options: a:Steering ability.,b:Braking distance.,c:Reaction distance.,d:Perception time.
note: Stopping distance depends on perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance; steering ability is not a direct component.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering interstate traffic from an entrance or acceleration ramp, who must yield?
options: a:The driver entering from the ramp should yield to traffic already on the interstate.,b:The drivers on the interstate must always yield.,c:You can force your way in if necessary.,d:Yielding is optional if you are already at highway speed.
note: Vehicles entering from a ramp must yield to traffic on the interstate and merge only when safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At dusk or on overcast days, you should:
options: a:Turn on your headlights (use low beams near other vehicles).,b:Only use parking lights.,c:Not turn on any lights until dark.,d:Use your high beams at all times for better visibility.
note: At dusk or in overcast conditions, turn on headlights and use low beams when within 1,000 feet of an oncoming vehicle or 500 feet of a vehicle you are following.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What color are pavement markings that separate traffic moving in opposite directions?
options: a:Yellow.,b:White.,c:Yellow and white.
note: Yellow centerlines separate traffic moving in opposite directions; white lines separate lanes moving the same way.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A steady yellow traffic signal means which color will soon appear?
options: a:Steady red.,b:Flashing red.,c:Steady green.,d:Flashing yellow.
note: A steady yellow warns that the signal is about to change to a steady red.

question: When should you always signal?
options: a:When turning, changing lanes, pulling into or out of a parking space, or pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.,b:Only when other drivers are nearby.,c:Only if you are turning left.,d:Signals are optional if roads are clear.
note: Always use your turn signal when turning, changing lanes, entering or exiting parking spaces, or pulling into traffic from an alley, driveway, or parking area, any time another road user could be affected by your movement.

question: After a serious motor vehicle crash, what is your immediate obligation?
options: a:Stop and, if possible, move your vehicle out of traffic; then render aid or call for help.,b:Only call the police.,c:Continue driving if damage seems minor.
note: After a serious crash, you must stop at the scene, help prevent further collisions by moving your vehicle out of traffic if it is safe and drivable, check for injuries, render reasonable aid, and call 911 or law enforcement as required by law.

question: If you pass your exit on the interstate, what should you do?
options: a:Make a U-turn on the highway median.,b:Quickly cut across lanes to reach the exit.,c:Continue driving and use the next exit to safely return to your route.
note: If you miss your exit on an interstate, continue to the next exit, then safely re-enter the highway in the opposite direction if needed. Never stop, back up, make a U-turn, or cut across the median or lanes to reach a missed exit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How do high speeds affect stopping distances and crash severity?
options: a:Higher speeds greatly increase stopping distance and crash severity.,b:High speeds reduce stopping distances.,c:Night driving only affects stopping distance, not speed.,d:Speeds have no effect on crash severity.
note: Driving faster increases the distance needed to stop and increases the force of impact in a collision, making crashes more severe.

question: What does a diamond-shaped traffic sign generally indicate?
options: a:An upcoming hazard or special condition ahead.,b:A nearby school zone.,c:A recreation area ahead.,d:A stop requirement.
note: Diamond-shaped signs are warning signs that alert drivers to existing or potential hazards or changes in road conditions ahead.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If traffic signals at an intersection are not functioning due to a power outage, how should you proceed?
options: a:Proceed as if you have the right-of-way.,b:Park and wait until power is restored.,c:Turn on your hazard lights and drive through without stopping.,d:Treat the intersection as a four-way stop
note: When signals are out, drivers should treat the intersection as a four-way stop and yield to vehicles that arrived before them or to the vehicle on the right if arriving simultaneously.

question: Which statement about winter driving is NOT true?
options: a:Checking antifreeze and washer fluid is important during winter.,b:Winter is often the most difficult driving season.,c:Snow tires can help improve traction on slippery roads.,d:Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
note: Do not use cruise control on snow, ice, or similar hazardous conditions. Winter driving requires extra caution and proactive vehicle maintenance.

question: How can you prevent drowsiness on long trips?
options: a:Slow down and drive more carefully,b:Turn up the car radio volume,c:Stop at regular intervals to rest and stretch
note: To prevent drowsiness on long trips, stop at regular intervals to rest, walk, and stretch. Slowing down, turning up the radio, or other “stay awake tricks” are not reliable or safe substitutes for rest.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic signal shows a green arrow with a red light, what does it mean?
options: a:You must wait for a solid green light to move in any direction.,b:You may proceed only in the direction indicated by the green arrow,c:You may go straight only.,d:You may turn in any direction after yielding.
note: A green arrow with a red light means you may proceed ONLY in the direction indicated by the green arrow, after yielding to pedestrians and other traffic in the intersection. The red light still applies to all other movements (such as going straight or turning in a different direction), which must remain stopped.

question: If you must drive in foggy weather, what is the correct lighting choice?
options: a:Turn on your hazard lights.,b:Drive at the posted maximum speed.,c:Turn on your low beam headlights.
note: In fog, use low beam headlights and reduce speed; high beams can reflect off the fog and reduce visibility, and hazard lights can confuse other drivers.

question: When is it appropriate to use your horn?
options: a:When you must stop quickly.,b:When passing another car routinely.,c:To alert others if you have lost control of your vehicle or to warn of imminent danger.,d:To express frustration at another driver.
note: Use your horn to warn others of immediate danger, such as when you lose control of your vehicle or to prevent a collision. Do not use the horn to express anger, as a routine signal, or without a safety-related reason.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a right turn on a green light, you must:
options: a:Always come to a complete stop before turning right on green.,b:Maintain your normal driving speed.,c:Stop and look for police vehicles only.,d:Yield to pedestrians and any traffic in the intersection before turning.
note: When making a right turn on a green light, you may proceed without stopping, but you must yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to any vehicles already in or lawfully entering the intersection. You should slow as needed, check for pedestrians and oncoming traffic, and complete the turn only when it is safe.

question: Before switching on the ignition, what safety step should you take?
options: a:Start the car then buckle up.,b:Be sure only backseat passengers are buckled.,c:Buckle your safety belt and ensure passengers are belted.,d:Make sure only adult passengers are belted.
note: Before switching on the ignition, you should buckle your safety belt and ensure that all passengers are properly belted. Making this a routine step improves safety for everyone in the vehicle.

question: If you are driving in another driver's blind spot, what should you do?
options: a:Flash your lights continuously.,b:Stay there; they should check mirrors.,c:Move forward or fall back so the other driver can see you.,d:Keep a steady pace in their blind spot.
note: If you find yourself driving in another driver's blind spot, adjust your speed to move forward or drop back so that you can be seen in their mirrors. Avoid staying in blind spots whenever possible.

question: When driving near heavy trucks, what must other drivers allow for?
options: a:That trucks make no noise at night.,b:The increased stopping distance required by large vehicles and the need to remain visible to their drivers.,c:That trucks will always yield to smaller vehicles.,d:That trucks can stop instantly.
note: When driving near heavy trucks, allow for their longer stopping distances and larger blind spots. Do not cut in front of them abruptly, and position your vehicle so that the truck driver can see you in their mirrors.

question: Who is most likely to be killed in a work zone crash?
options: a:Bicyclists.,b:Workers and flaggers.,c:Pedestrians on sidewalks.,d:Drivers and passengers.
note: Statistics show drivers and passengers are most likely to be killed in work zone crashes, so drive carefully.

question: If you hear a siren but do not immediately see the emergency vehicle, what should you do?
options: a:Pull safely to the right curb and stop until you can determine if it is approaching your street,b:Keep driving until you find it,c:Slow down but do not stop until you see it
note: If you hear a nearby siren but cannot locate the vehicle, safely pull over to the right side of the road and stop until you confirm it is not headed toward you.

question: Which road users are the hardest to see at night?
options: a:Other motorists.,b:Road signs.,c:Bicycles with lights on.,d:Pedestrians.
note: Pedestrians are hardest to see at night compared to signs or larger vehicles and require extra caution from drivers.

question: If you drink socially, what is a safe choice to ensure you get home safely?
options: a:Ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.,b:Drink coffee to sober up quickly.,c:Take a cold shower before driving.,d:Wait 5 minutes and drive home.
note: Arranging a sober ride home prevents driving impaired; coffee, cold showers, or short waits do not reduce blood alcohol concentration or make you safe to drive.

question: What do vehicle brake lights communicate to other drivers?
options: a:That you are slowing down or stopping,b:That you are making a turn,c:That your emergency brake is engaged
note: Brake lights signal to drivers behind that you are slowing down or stopping; keep them in working order.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an intersection requires a stop but has no stop line or crosswalk markings, where should you stop?
options: a:Only if you can see 200 feet in both directions.,b:At the nearest point before entering the intersecting roadway where you have a clear view of traffic.,c:In the middle of the intersection to get the best view.,d:You are not required to stop.
note: Stop at the nearest point before entering the intersecting roadway where you have a clear view of traffic, without moving into the intersection or cross traffic lanes.

question: How does smoking or preparing to smoke while driving affect driving?
options: a:It does not affect driving ability,b:It is a distracting activity that can take hands and eyes off the road,c:It helps keep drivers alert
note: Handling cigarettes or other smoking materials while driving is a distraction that can take your hands off the wheel and your eyes and attention off the road, increasing crash risk.

question: If you leave your vehicle unattended, what must you do?
options: a:Only set the parking brake,b:Leave it in neutral and unlocked,c:Turn off the engine
note: When leaving a vehicle unattended, you must stop the engine, remove the key, lock the ignition (or lock the vehicle), and set the parking brake. On a grade, you should also turn the wheels toward or away from the curb as appropriate. Simply turning off the engine alone is not sufficient, but among the given options, turning off the engine is the only partially correct choice.

question: On slippery roads you should:
options: a:Drive as you would on dry roads.,b:Use alternate routes only.,c:Increase your following distance to allow more stopping distance.,d:Follow the car ahead closely to avoid skids.
note: On slippery roads, you should reduce speed and increase your following distance to allow more time and space to stop safely. Do not follow other vehicles closely, and adjust your driving to the reduced traction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle on a two-lane road, when should you return to your lane?
options: a:Immediately after passing regardless of space.,b:Only if the other vehicle signals you to do so.,c:When there is enough room between you and the vehicle you passed.,d:At the next intersection.
note: After passing on a two-lane road, return to your lane only when you can see that there is enough space between you and the vehicle you passed and it is safe to move back without cutting in too closely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you find yourself already within an intersection when the light turns yellow, what should you do?
options: a:Stop immediately in the intersection.,b:Reverse out of the intersection quickly.,c:Honk to warn others and speed up.,d:Continue carefully through the intersection.
note: If a steady yellow appears while you are already in the intersection, you should continue through carefully rather than stopping abruptly in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a stop sign, after stopping you should look:
options: a:At your rearview mirror for tailgaters.,b:Only at the vehicle ahead and move when it moves.,c:Left first,d:Right first
note: At a stop sign, after stopping you should look left first, then right, and then left again, because traffic from the left is closer and usually poses the most immediate hazard.

question: How can you avoid being in a truck or bus driver's blind spot?
options: a:Drive as close behind as possible.,b:Never pass them under any circumstances.,c:Flash your lights to make them aware of you.,d:Avoid driving alongside them and do not tailgate.
note: Large trucks and buses have large blind spots on all sides. To avoid being in their blind spots, do not drive alongside them for long periods and do not follow too closely (tailgate).

question: Drivers may not pass from either direction when the centerline is:
options: a:Double solid yellow.,b:Combination solid and broken yellow.,c:Single broken yellow.
note: A double solid yellow centerline means vehicles traveling in either direction are not allowed to pass. Passing is prohibited from both directions.

question: How must drivers treat traffic signs and pavement markings?
options: a:They must always be obeyed.,b:They are only suggestions.,c:They apply only when other vehicles are present.,d:They can be ignored at night.
note: Traffic signs and pavement markings are traffic control devices and must be obeyed at all times to ensure safety and comply with the law.

question: If stopped at a railroad crossing that has more than one track, when should you begin to cross after a train passes?
options: a:Immediately after the first train clears your lane.,b:Only after you have a clear view down all tracks and are sure no other train is coming.,c:When traffic behind you starts moving.,d:As soon as the warning lights stop flashing.
note: At crossings with multiple tracks, wait until you can clearly see all tracks in both directions before proceeding; another train may be approaching on a different track.

question: Compared to daytime driving, how dangerous is driving at night?
options: a:Less dangerous due to less traffic.,b:More dangerous,c:No different in danger level.,d:Safer if you use high beams.
note: Night driving is more hazardous due to decreased visibility, headlight glare, and a higher likelihood of tired or impaired drivers.

question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, what is required?
options: a:Pull to the right curb and stop to allow it to pass.,b:Slow down and keep moving in your lane.,c:Continue at the same speed and ignore it.,d:Speed up to get out of its way.
note: When an emergency vehicle using lights and/or siren approaches from either direction, you must immediately yield the right-of-way by pulling as close as possible to the right-hand edge or curb of the roadway and stopping, clear of any intersection, until the emergency vehicle has passed. If you are already in an intersection, continue through it and then pull over to the right and stop as soon as it is safe.

question: Which technique helps avoid crashes on icy or snowy roads?
options: a:Drive as close as possible to other vehicles for wind protection.,b:Engage four-wheel drive and accelerate more.,c:Reduce speed and increase following distance.,d:Use cruise control to maintain constant speed.
note: Slowing down and increasing following distance are the most important steps to reduce crash risk on icy or snowy roads.

question: Which strategy best avoids alcohol-related crashes?
options: a:Drink water between alcoholic drinks and drive carefully.,b:Accept drinks but refuse to drive only if you feel drunk.,c:Call a friend who will let you drive anyway.,d:Decide before you start drinking that you will not drive and arrange an alternative ride.
note: The most effective way to prevent alcohol-related crashes is to decide in advance not to drive and arrange a safe alternative before drinking.

question: Two solid white lines across a lane mark a crosswalk. What must drivers do?
options: a:Drive through if no pedestrians are visible.,b:Yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and give them the right-of-way.,c:Pedestrians must yield to vehicles.,d:Only stop for pedestrians if accompanied by a guard.
note: When pedestrians are in a marked crosswalk, vehicles must stop and yield until the crosswalk is clear.

question: Which statement about alcohol and skills is accurate?
options: a:Alcohol improves driving at low doses.,b:Only BACs above the legal limit cause impairment.,c:Alcohol affects only reaction time.,d:Even small amounts of alcohol can reduce concentration
note: Even small amounts of alcohol impair cognitive and driving skills; no amount is safe for driving.

question: How does eating or drinking while driving affect your driving?
options: a:It causes no driving errors.,b:It makes you a better driver because you are not hungry.,c:It distracts you and makes it harder to stay in your lane and control the vehicle.
note: Eating, drinking, or smoking while driving takes hands and eyes off the road and increases the chance of lane drift and loss of control.

question: What helps a person overcome the effects of alcohol?
options: a:Hot coffee.,b:Time only; nothing like coffee or fresh air will sober someone quickly.,c:Drinking tomato juice and lime.,d:Fresh air and cold water.
note: Only the passage of time allows the body to eliminate alcohol; remedies like coffee or fresh air do not speed sobriety.

question: Which substances can impair driving and lead to DUII arrest?
options: a:Only illegal drugs.,b:Alcohol.,c:Only alcoholic beverages.,d:Only large amounts of sugar-rich drinks.
note: Alcohol is one of several substances that can impair driving and lead to DUI/DUII arrest. Illegal drugs, inhalants, marijuana, and some prescription or over‑the‑counter medications can also impair driving. However, among the listed options, alcohol (choice b) is the only substance that actually can lead to DUII arrest, so b is the best answer to this specific set of choices.

question: A person carrying a white cane or using a guide dog is most likely:
options: a:Blind or visually impaired and should be yielded to.,b:Participating in a traffic study.,c:Deaf and unable to hear horns.,d:Training for a marathon.
note: Drivers must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians who are blind or visually impaired and using a white cane or guide dog.

question: When must you stop for a pedestrian?
options: a:Only in clearly marked crosswalks with lights.,b:When the pedestrian is in a marked or unmarked crosswalk.,c:Only when a crossing guard is present.,d:Only if they are on your side of the road.
note: You must yield and, if necessary, stop for pedestrians in both marked and unmarked crosswalks at intersections.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the meaning of a green arrow in a traffic signal?
options: a:You may only proceed if accompanied by a circular green light.,b:It is a warning for cyclists only.,c:It is used only on one-way streets.,d:It has the same meaning as a circular green but requires you to move only in the direction shown by the arrow.
note: A green arrow means you have a protected movement in the direction of the arrow. You may proceed only in the direction shown by the arrow, after yielding to any vehicles or pedestrians already in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on a freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Stop immediately and wait for traffic to clear.,b:Make a U-turn across lanes.,c:Back up on the shoulder to reach the exit.,d:Continue to the next exit and safely turn around; do not back up or stop.
note: If you miss your exit on a freeway, continue to the next exit and safely turn around. Do not stop, back up, or make a U-turn on the freeway or its shoulder.

question: You may pass another vehicle when the line dividing lanes is which type of line?
options: a:Solid yellow line.,b:Double solid yellow.,c:Broken white line.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction and may be crossed to change lanes when safe. Passing another vehicle traveling in the same direction is permitted when you can safely move into an adjacent lane marked with a broken white line. (Note: Passing on two-way roads is typically governed by yellow lines, which are not offered as an option here.)

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where should your car be positioned when making a right turn?
options: a:Near the center of the street.,b:Close to the left side of the street.,c:As close to the right side of the street as possible.
note: When preparing to make a right turn, move as far to the right as safely possible and do not cut across lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you drive much slower than the posted speed and hold up traffic, what is required of you?
options: a:You may refuse to let others pass you at any time.,b:If you are impeding traffic you must pull off the road and let other vehicles pass.,c:You should always stay in the left lane.,d:You are always safer than faster drivers.
note: Driving significantly slower than the flow of traffic can be hazardous. If you are impeding or blocking traffic, you are generally required to move to the right and, when necessary and safe, pull off the road or into a turnout to let other vehicles pass.

question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
options: a:New drivers only.,b:Human error (driver mistakes).,c:Bad weather alone.,d:Vehicle defects only.
note: Most traffic crashes are caused by human error—mistakes in observation, judgment, or vehicle control—rather than by weather or vehicle defects alone.

question: What action best ensures safety when backing a vehicle?
options: a:Walk behind the vehicle to check for children and obstacles before getting in.,b:Check rearview mirrors only after getting in.,c:Honk immediately before reversing.,d:Back quickly and rely on mirrors.
note: Because backing limits visibility, always check behind the vehicle before entering it and before you back up.

question: At a railroad crossing where you do not see or hear a train, you must stop when:
options: a:Only if your passenger says to stop.,b:A stop sign is posted.,c:If the crossing is on a hill.,d:A train might come in an hour.
note: You must stop at a railroad crossing when required by a stop sign, gates, flashing red lights, a flagger’s signal, or when a train is visible, sounding a warning, or close enough to be an immediate hazard.

question: Which of these does NOT promote safe night driving?
options: a:Keep your windshield clean,b:Be aware that tinted windows reduce night visibility,c:Carry a flashlight in your vehicle
note: While a flashlight can be useful to have in the vehicle for emergencies, it does not directly improve your ability to see the road while driving at night. Keeping your windshield clean and being aware that tinted windows reduce night visibility are both directly related to safe night driving.

question: Which statement is true about seat belts and child restraints?
options: a:Never place a rear-facing infant seat in the front seat of a vehicle with an airbag.,b:Airbags can be dangerous to infants or small children even in low-speed collisions.,c:Always make sure every passenger is using a seat belt or appropriate child restraint.,d:Seat belts are optional for adults on short trips.
note: Never place a rear-facing infant seat in the front seat of a vehicle with an active passenger airbag. Infants and small children should ride properly restrained in the rear seat. Airbags can be dangerous to infants and small children, and all occupants should use seat belts or appropriate child restraints on every trip.

question: After stopping for a school bus unloading children, what should you do before proceeding?
options: a:Accelerate quickly to clear the area.,b:Honk to alert children to get out of the way.,c:Watch for children walking along the road and proceed with extreme caution.,d:Wait until each child waves to you.
note: You must remain stopped for a school bus with flashing red lights and an extended stop arm until the lights stop flashing, the stop arm is withdrawn, and the bus starts moving or the driver signals you to proceed. After that, watch carefully for children walking along or crossing the road and proceed with extreme caution.

question: When are roads most slippery during a rainfall?
options: a:Only when temperatures are below freezing.,b:After it has been raining for an hour or more.,c:The day after it rains.,d:During the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.
note: Roads are most slippery during the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm because oil and other residues on the road surface mix with the water and rise to the surface, reducing traction. After it has rained for a while, much of this residue is washed away and conditions usually improve, though they can still be hazardous.

question: What is the key rule about speed management when approaching curves?
options: a:Slow down before entering the curve to maintain control.,b:Keep posted speed on entry and slow at the sharpest point.,c:Accelerate gently before the curve.,d:Brake hard in the curve for best traction.
note: You should slow down before entering a curve so you can maintain control throughout the turn. Braking hard in the curve can cause skidding, and entering too fast reduces your ability to stay in your lane and react to hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a narrow road when you meet an oncoming vehicle, you must:
options: a:Pull completely off the road and stop.,b:Allow the oncoming vehicle at least one-half of the main-traveled portion of the road.,c:Pass on the shoulder immediately.,d:Demand the other driver back up.
note: On a narrow road, you must yield at least one-half of the main-traveled portion of the roadway to oncoming traffic so both vehicles can pass safely. You are not generally required to pull completely off the road and stop unless necessary to avoid a collision or where the roadway is too narrow for both vehicles to remain on the pavement.

question: When riding in a vehicle, how should small children be secured?
options: a:A strong adult can hold a child safely during a trip.,b:Children should ride without restraints on short trips only.,c:Children may stand on the back floor if supervised.,d:Children must be properly secured in an appropriate child seat or seat belt for their size and age.
note: Children must be properly secured in an appropriate child safety seat, booster seat, or seat belt that is suitable for their size and age. It is unsafe and illegal in most jurisdictions for an adult to hold a child instead of using proper restraints.

question: If your vehicle has anti-lock brakes (ABS) and starts to lose traction, what should you do with the brake pedal?
options: a:Pump the brakes rapidly.,b:Release the brake and downshift immediately.,c:Press and hold the gas pedal.,d:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly while steering to safety.
note: If your vehicle has anti-lock brakes (ABS) and you start to lose traction, you should press and hold the brake pedal firmly while steering in the desired direction. The ABS system will automatically pump the brakes to help maintain steering control; you should not pump the brakes yourself.

question: What does a solid white line between lanes on a multi-lane road mean?
options: a:It separates lanes moving in opposite directions and passing is not allowed,b:It separates lanes moving in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe,c:It separates lanes moving in the same direction and passing is not allowed
note: White lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. A solid white line indicates that lane changes are discouraged or, in some situations, prohibited, so you should generally not change lanes across it.

question: When must you dim your high beams for an oncoming vehicle to avoid blinding the other driver?
options: a:When the oncoming vehicle is within 450 feet.,b:When the oncoming vehicle is within 400 feet.,c:When the oncoming vehicle is within 500 feet.
note: You must dim your high beams when an oncoming vehicle is within about 500 feet to avoid blinding the other driver. This distance is the standard requirement in many US jurisdictions.

question: When an emergency vehicle is using sirens or flashing lights, drivers must:
options: a:Ignore it unless it is directly behind you.,b:Follow directly behind the emergency vehicle closely to clear the way.,c:Yield the right-of-way and pull over to allow it to pass.,d:Speed up to avoid delay.
note: Yield to police, fire, or ambulance vehicles using sirens or flashing lights by pulling to the right edge of the road and stopping until they have passed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is passing unlawful and unsafe?
options: a:Only at intersections.,b:On hills,c:Only on hills and curves.,d:Only at railroad crossings.
note: Passing is unlawful and unsafe in several locations, including on hills and curves where you cannot see far enough ahead, at intersections, and at railroad crossings. Among the given options, the best answer is that passing is unlawful and unsafe on hills.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about speed is true?
options: a:Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous as well as speeding.,b:Speeding is never dangerous if you are an experienced driver.,c:You can drive at any speed if no one is around.,d:Higher speed always reduces crash severity.
note: Both excessive speed and driving much slower than the flow of traffic can create hazards. Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous, and higher speeds increase both crash risk and crash severity.

question: If your right wheels leave the pavement, what is the correct action to take?
options: a:Stop immediately where you are.,b:Pull sharply back onto the road and accelerate.,c:Take your foot off the accelerator,d:Turn the steering wheel hard left to regain the road quickly.
note: If your right wheels leave the pavement, do not jerk the wheel or accelerate. Take your foot off the accelerator, steer straight, slow down gradually, and when the road is clear, gently steer back onto the pavement.

question: If another driver is tailgating you, what should you do?
options: a:Move over to the right if there is an open lane; if not, wait until the road ahead is clear and reduce your speed slowly to encourage them to pass.,b:Brake abruptly to warn them.,c:Increase your speed to create distance.,d:Ignore them and continue your current speed.
note: If another driver is tailgating you, move over to the right if there is an open lane. If you cannot change lanes, wait until the road ahead is clear and gradually reduce your speed to encourage the tailgater to pass. Do not brake abruptly or speed up.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging into a crowded freeway, what steps should you take?
options: a:Drive on the shoulder briefly to find a gap.,b:Stop at the end of the ramp then pull out when clear.,c:Enter slowly and expect traffic to stop for you.,d:Use mirrors and blind-spot checks
note: Adjust speed on the entrance ramp to match freeway traffic, check mirrors and blind spots, and yield as needed when merging.

question: What are common causes of distracted driving?
options: a:Looking at the road ahead.,b:Driving with both hands on the wheel.,c:Using turn signals.,d:Eating
note: Common causes of distracted driving include any non-driving tasks that take your attention away from the road, such as eating, texting, using a phone, adjusting controls, or interacting with passengers. Looking at the road ahead, using turn signals, and driving with both hands on the wheel are not distractions.

question: When driving in rain, which lights should you use?
options: a:Parking lights only.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:High beam headlights.,d:High beams and hazard lights.
note: In rainy conditions, you should use low beam headlights to improve your visibility and help other drivers see you. High beams can reflect off rain, fog, or snow and reduce your ability to see. Parking lights alone are not sufficient and are illegal to use as a substitute for headlights while driving in most states.

question: To check your blind spot before changing lanes to the left, where should you glance?
options: a:Only at your side mirror.,b:At the center console.,c:Over your left shoulder.,d:Over your right shoulder.
note: Glance over the shoulder toward the lane you intend to enter to check blind spots.

question: What is the ''No zone'' around a large truck or bus?
options: a:A place where stereo use is restricted,b:The vehicle's blind spots where the truck driver cannot see other vehicles,c:A special reduced-speed zone
note: Large trucks and buses have blind areas on all sides where smaller vehicles disappear from the driver's view; avoid lingering in these zones.

question: If an oncoming vehicle fails to dim high beams, where should you glance?
options: a:At the vehicle's wheels,b:Toward the left side of the road,c:Toward the right side of the road
note: Look slightly toward the right edge of your lane (the right side of the road) to avoid being blinded by the high beams while still keeping enough view of the roadway.

question: On a one-way street when an emergency vehicle using flashing lights approaches you, what must you do?
options: a:Drive toward the nearest roadside and stop.,b:Speed up and take the nearest exit.,c:Drive with your flashers turned on.
note: When an emergency vehicle using flashing lights and/or a siren approaches you on a one-way street, you must drive toward the nearest roadside or curb and stop until the emergency vehicle has passed, unless otherwise directed by a police officer.

question: Highway signs that require drivers to obey instructions are called:
options: a:Warning signs.,b:Information signs.,c:Regulatory signs.
note: Regulatory signs give instructions that must be obeyed, such as speed limits, stop, yield, and no-turn signs. Failure to comply can result in citations or other penalties.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you want to turn left at an intersection but oncoming traffic is heavy, what may you do if the light is green?
options: a:Turn on red if it seems safe.,b:Use the next intersection to turn.,c:Wait behind the crosswalk until traffic clears.,d:Enter the intersection and wait in the center to complete your left turn when it is safe (only if the light is green and the way is clear).
note: If the light is green and oncoming traffic is heavy, you may carefully enter the intersection and wait near the center, keeping your wheels straight, and complete your left turn when there is a safe gap or when the light changes and oncoming traffic stops, as long as you do not block cross traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you yield to other drivers when entering the roadway?
options: a:Only when your traffic signal is a green arrow.,b:When entering from a garage,c:When they are on a road to your left at an unmarked intersection and you arrived first.
note: You must yield to drivers and pedestrians when entering a roadway from a driveway, garage, alley, or private road. Stop before the sidewalk or edge of the roadway and proceed only when it is safe.

question: If your car breaks down on a highway, what should you do?
options: a:Leave the vehicle in traffic and walk away.,b:Sound your horn repeatedly at passing motorists.,c:Sit in the car and wait without signaling.,d:Signal and move your vehicle as far off the road as safely possible, then turn on hazard flashers and use warning devices if available.
note: If your car breaks down on a highway, signal and move as far off the roadway as safely possible (preferably onto the right shoulder). Turn on your hazard flashers, raise the hood or place warning devices (flares/triangles) if available and safe to do so, and stay away from moving traffic. Do not leave the vehicle stopped in a traffic lane.

question: If another driver is passing you, what should you do to help them pass safely?
options: a:Speed up to prevent them from passing.,b:Pull off the road.,c:Signal to them when it is safe to pass.,d:Check for oncoming traffic and maintain or slightly adjust your speed to let them re-enter safely.
note: If another driver is passing you, stay in your lane, maintain or slightly reduce your speed if needed, and check for oncoming traffic so you are aware of conditions. Adjust your speed slightly if necessary to allow the passing vehicle to re-enter your lane safely. Do not speed up, pull off the road unnecessarily, or signal them when it is safe to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you go through an intersection that has a stop sign but no stop line or crosswalk?
options: a:After stopping at least 20 feet before the intersection.,b:After slowing down and checking for cross traffic.,c:After coming to a complete stop before entering and ensuring it is safe.
note: If there is no stop line or crosswalk at a stop sign, you must come to a complete stop before entering the intersection, at the point nearest the intersecting roadway where you have a clear view of approaching traffic, and proceed only when it is safe.

question: If you are stopped in the intersection waiting to make a left turn, how should your wheels be positioned?
options: a:Signal and keep wheels turned to the left.,b:Flash your headlights to alert drivers behind you.,c:Keep your wheels straight while signaling; do not have wheels turned to the left.
note: When waiting in an intersection to make a left turn, keep your wheels straight while signaling. This prevents a rear-end collision from pushing your vehicle into oncoming traffic.

question: What do regulatory traffic signs tell drivers?
options: a:About conditions near the road,b:Directions to nearby towns,c:What a driver must or must not do
note: Regulatory signs tell drivers what they must or must not do. They indicate traffic laws and regulations, such as speed limits, parking restrictions, and turn prohibitions.

question: Pentagonal traffic signs are used to indicate:
options: a:No passing zones.,b:School zones and school crossings.,c:Speed limits.,d:Railroad crossings.
note: A five-sided (pentagonal) sign indicates a school zone or school crossing; be alert for children and pedestrians.

question: You need to back out of your driveway and children are nearby. What should you do first?
options: a:Rev the engine to get their attention.,b:Sound your horn to warn the children.,c:Get out and walk to the back of the car to be sure the way is clear.,d:Check the side mirror only and proceed.
note: Before backing into or out of a driveway, especially when children are nearby, you should get out and check behind the vehicle to be sure the way is clear, because children can be hard to see from the driver's seat.

question: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, what must you do?
options: a:Drive with your flashers on,b:Slow down until it passes,c:Pull over to the side and stop
note: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, you must immediately yield the right-of-way by pulling as close as possible to the right-hand curb or edge of the roadway and stopping until the emergency vehicle has passed. Do not stop in an intersection; clear the intersection first, then pull over and stop.

question: If you are involved in an accident, what should you do at the scene?
options: a:Leave immediately if damage is minor.,b:Stop at or near the scene.,c:Stand in traffic to warn other drivers.,d:Drive to the nearest gas station before reporting.
note: If you are involved in an accident, you must stop at or near the scene. If possible and safe, move vehicles out of the flow of traffic, turn off ignitions of damaged vehicles, turn on hazard flashers, and avoid standing in traffic lanes. Exchange information and, where required by law, notify law enforcement and/or file a report.

question: How should you pass a bicyclist safely?
options: a:Flash your lights to tell them to move over.,b:Honk to alert them and pass quickly.,c:Slow down and give the bicyclist as much room as possible.,d:Use the bicycle lane to get around them.
note: Slow down and pass the bicyclist only when it is safe, giving them as much room as possible. In many states, you must leave at least 3 feet of clearance (or more, as required by local law). Do not honk unnecessarily, crowd the bicyclist, or drive in a bicycle lane to pass.

question: How should drivers treat a flashing red traffic light?
options: a:As an indication to yield only to pedestrians.,b:As a stop sign — come to a full stop and proceed when safe.,c:As a warning to speed up.,d:As a green light if no traffic is present.
note: A flashing red signal requires a full stop and then proceeding when it is safe, just like a stop sign.

question: When parking downhill on a two-way street, which way should you turn your wheels?
options: a:Keep wheels straight.,b:Turn your wheels to the left.,c:Turn your wheels to the right (toward the curb).
note: When parked facing downhill, turn the wheels toward the curb so the vehicle will roll into the curb if it moves.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Who must wear a safety belt while a vehicle is moving in Oregon?
options: a:Nobody,b:Only passengers under age 16,c:The driver and all passengers
note: Oregon law requires the driver and all passengers to use safety belts or child safety restraints, regardless of seating position, with limited exceptions (such as certain medical exemptions and specific vehicle types). Belts are your best protection in a crash.

question: At a school crossing sign, how should a driver behave?
options: a:Always come to a complete stop no matter what.,b:Speed through quickly to clear the area.,c:Watch for children,d:Sound your horn whenever children are nearby.
note: When you see a school crossing sign, be alert for children and be prepared to stop; always yield to pedestrians in crosswalks.

question: What does the slow-moving vehicle emblem look like?
options: a:A reflective orange triangle (warning of slow-moving vehicles).,b:A rectangular red sign.,c:A diamond-shaped yellow sign.,d:A circular green sign.
note: The slow-moving vehicle emblem is a reflective orange triangle; vehicles displaying it typically travel at 25 mph or slower.

question: Why should you be especially alert to motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?
options: a:They follow completely different traffic laws.,b:They always have the right-of-way in all situations.,c:They are smaller and harder to see and may move unpredictably,d:They are required to yield to you at all times.
note: Smaller road users such as motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians can be harder to detect and may move unexpectedly; drivers must be especially alert to their presence to prevent collisions.

question: Guide signs are what color and what information do they provide?
options: a:Red — regulatory prohibitions.,b:Blue — destination services.,c:Green — directional and mileage information.,d:Yellow — general warnings.
note: Guide or destination signs are typically green with white letters and provide directions, routes, and distances to locations.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a heavy truck from behind on an uphill grade, what should you expect?
options: a:The truck driver must pull over to let you pass.,b:The truck may be traveling slower than the posted speed and it may be unlawful to pass on a hill where visibility is limited.,c:The truck will always stay at posted speed.,d:You can safely pass on the left at any time.
note: Large trucks often slow down on uphill grades and may travel below the posted speed. Passing on a hill where your view is limited by curves or crests is often illegal and always risky, so you should expect slower speed and be cautious about passing.

question: When stopped on an uphill slope, why allow extra space in front of your vehicle?
options: a:Because intersections are dangerous,b:Because a stop sign is likely ahead,c:Because the vehicle ahead may roll backward when traffic moves again
note: When stopped on an uphill slope, the vehicle ahead may roll backward slightly when starting to move again. Leaving extra space reduces the risk of a rear-end collision if this happens.

question: What is the only reliable way to reduce your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Allow time for your body to metabolize the alcohol.,b:Drink coffee to sober up.,c:Exercise to burn off alcohol.
note: The only reliable way to reduce your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is to allow time for your body to metabolize the alcohol. Coffee, exercise, cold showers, or other tricks do not speed up this process or lower your BAC.

question: How should drivers treat railroad crossings?
options: a:As safe places to park briefly,b:As safe to cross because trains are rare,c:As potentially dangerous—always look and listen for trains
note: Railroad crossings are always potentially dangerous; obey signals, look both ways, and never cross until it is clearly safe.

question: If your power steering fails while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Brake hard and park in the lane.,b:Work harder to steer,c:Ignore it and continue until the next exit.,d:Turn off the ignition immediately.
note: If power steering stops, you will need more effort to steer; slow down, steer carefully to a safe place off the roadway, and stop to address the problem.

question: Which of these helps reduce road rage and aggressive driving?
options: a:Obey speed limits and use turn signals,b:Allow extra travel time,c:All of the above
note: Allowing extra travel time, obeying speed limits, and using turn signals all help reduce stress, prevent rushing, and lower the chance of road rage or aggressive driving. Since both listed behaviors are helpful, the best answer is "All of the above."

question: Before moving into the left lane from the right on a multilane highway, what checks should you make?
options: a:Check mirrors, look over your left shoulder for the blind spot, and signal before changing lanes.,b:Rely only on the rearview mirror.,c:Turn on your hazard lights and change lanes quickly.,d:Honk to warn other drivers before merging.
note: Always check mirrors and the blind spot by looking over your shoulder, and signal each lane change to alert other drivers.

question: When you hear or see an approaching emergency vehicle on a divided multilane highway, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down, move to open a clear path, and stop if necessary.,b:Ignore it if other lanes are available.,c:Stop instantly in your lane wherever you are.,d:Speed up to clear the left lane.
note: Provide a clear path for emergency vehicles by slowing and moving to create space; on most roads you should move right and stop if necessary. Do not try to outdrive or block the emergency vehicle.

question: Which color typically indicates areas of public recreation or cultural interest on highway signs?
options: a:Green.,b:Orange.,c:Brown.,d:Red.
note: Brown signs are used to indicate areas of public recreation or historical/cultural interest. Green signs are generally used for guide information such as directions and distances, and orange is used for temporary work zones.

question: What is a risk of drinking alcohol while taking medication?
options: a:It will reduce the impact of the drug,b:It cures your illness,c:It can increase the effects of both substances
note: Alcohol and many medications interact to strengthen impairment and health risks; avoid combining them before driving.

question: Where should you keep a space cushion around your vehicle?
options: a:Only in front of your vehicle.,b:Only behind your vehicle.,c:On all sides of your vehicle (front, rear, left and right).,d:Only on the sides when parked.
note: Keeping a buffer of space on all sides gives you time to react to hazards and reduces the chance of collisions.

question: What does a flashing red light at an intersection indicate?
options: a:You should slow down and continue without stopping.,b:The signal is malfunctioning and can be ignored.,c:You may proceed without stopping if no other vehicles are present.,d:You must stop completely and yield; it is the same as a stop sign.
note: A flashing red light requires a complete stop, yielding to other traffic and pedestrians before proceeding when safe.

question: When passing a bicyclist on a two-lane road with no bicycle lane, what is the safest approach?
options: a:Sound your horn and pass closely.,b:Slow down and pass only when it is safe, allowing at least 3 feet of clearance.,c:Expect the bicyclist to move over and maintain your speed.,d:Pass only at traffic signals or stop signs.
note: When passing a bicyclist on a two-lane road with no bicycle lane, slow down and pass only when it is safe, leaving at least 3 feet of clearance (or more at higher speeds or for groups of cyclists). Do not sound your horn unnecessarily or pass closely.

question: Which statement about passing motorcycles is true?
options: a:Motorcycles do not need a full lane.,b:It is okay for drivers to follow motorcycles closely.,c:The driver of a passenger vehicle must change lanes completely when passing a motorcycle to give it full lane width.,d:A motorcycle with two people is more stable than with one.
note: When passing a motorcycle, you must move completely into the adjacent lane so the motorcycle has the entire lane width; do not share a lane with it. Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane, and you should not follow them too closely because they can stop more quickly and are more vulnerable in a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are waiting to turn left at a multilane intersection and opposing traffic blocks your view, what should you do?
options: a:Accelerate rapidly when the first lane is clear.,b:Turn on your hazard lights and proceed slowly.,c:Enter the intersection and wait for a wave from oncoming traffic.,d:Wait until you can see all lanes you must cross before making the turn.
note: If opposing traffic blocks your view when you are waiting to turn left at a multilane intersection, you must wait until you can clearly see all lanes you must cross and can complete the turn safely. Do not accelerate rapidly into a lane you cannot see, and do not rely on other drivers to signal you through.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it legal to pass another vehicle on the right?
options: a:Only when the other driver signals you to pass.,b:When the road narrows such as on a bridge.,c:Whenever you can,d:When the other vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is a proper lane available to pass.
note: You may pass on the right when the vehicle ahead is waiting or signaling to turn left and there is a proper lane available for passing, or on a multilane roadway with two or more lanes moving in the same direction. You must not pass on the right by driving off the pavement or the main-traveled portion of the road.

question: Compared with smaller vehicles, larger vehicles generally have:
options: a:Smaller blind spots.,b:Larger blind spots.,c:Blind spots only in the front.,d:No blind spots.
note: Large vehicles such as trucks, buses, and SUVs generally have larger blind spots than smaller vehicles. These blind spots are often directly behind, along the sides, and sometimes in front of the vehicle, requiring extra caution when passing or following.

question: If you're angry after an incident at work, what should you do before driving home?
options: a:Take a few minutes to calm down before starting to drive.,b:Play loud music to forget about it.,c:Drive fast to let off steam.,d:Call someone and drive while talking.
note: If you are angry or emotionally upset, you should take time to calm down before driving. Strong emotions can impair judgment, increase risk-taking, and lead to aggressive driving. Do not use driving itself, loud music, or phone conversations as a way to cope while behind the wheel.

question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?
options: a:Passing is allowed from the lane next to the broken line only,b:Passing is allowed from the lane next to the solid line,c:Passing is permitted from either direction
note: When a broken yellow line is adjacent to a solid yellow line, passing is allowed only for drivers traveling on the side with the broken line, and only when it is safe to do so. Drivers on the solid-line side may not pass.

question: Traffic lanes moving in opposite directions are separated by what color lines?
options: a:White.,b:Black.,c:Red.,d:Yellow.
note: Yellow center lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. White lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If turning left onto a one-way street, into which lane should you turn?
options: a:The bicycle lane even if marked.,b:The lane closest to your previous lane (leftmost of the destination lanes).,c:Either lane randomly.,d:The right lane because it may be clearer.
note: When turning left onto a one-way street, you must turn into the lane closest to you in the direction of travel—typically the leftmost lane of the one-way street, unless signs or lane markings direct otherwise.

question: A leaking exhaust system can cause what effect on a driver?
options: a:Prevent your headlights from working.,b:Improve fuel economy.,c:Cause your engine to overheat instantly.,d:Make you drowsy or cause poisoning while driving.
note: A leaking exhaust system can allow carbon monoxide and other toxic fumes to enter the vehicle’s interior, which can make you drowsy, impair your driving, or even cause poisoning and death. It should be repaired immediately.

question: An advisory speed sign attached to a curve means you should:
options: a:Ignore it when it is raining.,b:Reduce your speed below the posted limit in poor weather or road conditions.,c:Follow it only on highways.
note: An advisory speed sign on a curve indicates the recommended maximum speed for that curve under ideal conditions. In poor weather or bad road conditions, you should slow down even further below both the posted speed limit and the advisory speed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following describes correct passing procedures?
options: a:Use your horn instead of signaling.,b:Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes.,c:Merge back only after you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,d:Signal only if another car is beside you.
note: When passing, you must signal before changing lanes (in most states at least 100 feet before the maneuver), check your mirrors and blind spots, pass safely, and do not return to your original lane until you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

question: If the driver ahead seems distracted (one hand on wheel, talking), what should you do?
options: a:Tailgate to encourage attention.,b:Give the vehicle extra space and be prepared for unpredictable actions.,c:Pass immediately on the right regardless of safety.,d:Follow their example since they know the route.
note: Allow extra following distance for distracted drivers because they are more likely to make mistakes.

question: How can stress affect your driving?
options: a:By reducing your ability to concentrate on driving tasks.,b:By decreasing your chances of being in an accident.,c:By making you fall asleep at the wheel.
note: Strong emotions or stress reduce your ability to concentrate and impair driving decisions; it is safer to delay driving if you are emotionally unstable.

question: What should you do to be safe when crossing railroad tracks?
options: a:Never try to beat a train; if a train is approaching or warning devices are active, stop and wait.,b:Look only when lights are flashing.,c:Look and listen in both directions, obey all warning devices, and proceed only when it is safe and you can completely clear the tracks.
note: Before crossing tracks, always look and listen for trains from both directions, obey all warning signs, signals, and gates, and proceed only when you are sure it is safe and there is enough room to fully clear the tracks.

question: Why must you be especially alert for motorcycles?
options: a:They always travel slower than traffic.,b:They do not use headlights at night.,c:They rarely obey traffic laws.,d:They are smaller and harder to see and may be hidden in blind spots.
note: Motorcycles are harder to see, may be hidden in blind spots, and their speed and distance may be harder to judge, so you must be especially alert for them.

question: What does a yellow and black diamond-shaped sign indicate?
options: a:Traffic laws and regulations,b:Directions to cities and towns ahead,c:Warning—hazards or conditions on or near the road ahead
note: Diamond-shaped yellow signs warn drivers of potential hazards or changes in road conditions so they can take appropriate action.

question: How does being distracted while driving affect your reactions to hazards?
options: a:It only affects new drivers.,b:It makes you react faster.,c:It usually slows your reaction time and increases crash risk.,d:It has no effect on your driving.
note: Distractions reduce drivers' ability to perceive and respond to hazards, usually slowing reaction time and increasing the likelihood of a crash.

question: If you're involved in a crash and your vehicle blocks traffic, what should you do?
options: a:Leave it and walk away to safety.,b:Wait for the police before attempting to move it.,c:Never move your vehicle under any circumstances.,d:Move your vehicle off the traveled portion of the roadway if possible.
note: If you are involved in a minor crash and your vehicle is drivable, you should move it off the traveled portion of the roadway if possible and safe to do so, then exchange information and wait for authorities if required.

question: Which actions should you take when changing lanes on a highway?
options: a:Signal only if other cars are present.,b:Signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder before changing lanes.,c:Check mirrors only and then quickly move.,d:Change lanes without signaling if it’s safe.
note: Before changing lanes, you must always signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder. Do not rely on signaling alone.

question: When a traffic signal turns green, what must you do first?
options: a:Back up slowly if the path is blocked.,b:Accelerate as quickly as possible.,c:Honk to warn cross traffic.,d:Yield the right-of-way to any pedestrians or vehicles still in the intersection.
note: A green light means you may go only after yielding the right-of-way to pedestrians and any vehicles still in the intersection.

question: What can impair a person's ability to drive safely besides alcohol?
options: a:Eating food while driving.,b:Only alcohol affects driving ability.,c:Certain medications,d:Wearing sunglasses.
note: Driving ability can be reduced by alcohol, legal and illegal drugs, and drowsiness from lack of sleep.

question: If you begin feeling tired while driving, what is the best action?
options: a:Open a window to get fresh air and continue.,b:Turn up the radio and speed up.,c:Stop driving and take a break or rest.,d:Drink coffee and keep driving.
note: Fatigue impairs driving similar to alcohol; the proper response is to stop and rest rather than continue driving.

question: Which of the following is true about cellphone use while driving in Oregon?
options: a:Drivers 18 and older are prohibited from texting while driving but may handhold for calls.,b:Drivers under 18 may talk but not text while driving.,c:Drivers under 18 may not talk or text while driving; drivers 18+ must use hands-free when talking.
note: In Oregon, drivers under 18 may not use a phone to talk or text while driving. Drivers 18 and older may not text and must use a hands-free accessory if they talk on a phone while driving.

question: What documents must a driver produce when stopped for a traffic violation or equipment check?
options: a:Only insurance card.,b:Only their license.,c:Driver license, vehicle registration, and proof of insurance.,d:Only the vehicle title.
note: When stopped for a traffic violation or equipment check, a driver must be able to provide their driver license, proof of vehicle registration, and proof of insurance. The question stem and options should reflect that more than just the license is required.

question: A downward-facing triangular sign typically means:
options: a:Yield to other traffic.,b:No U-turn.,c:School zone ahead.,d:Construction ahead.
note: A downward-pointing triangular sign is the standard shape for a YIELD sign. It tells drivers to slow down and yield the right-of-way to other traffic and pedestrians.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What can happen to a bicyclist who fails to obey traffic laws?
options: a:They are legally required to ride on the sidewalk instead.,b:They will always receive only a warning.,c:They may be cited or ticketed like other road users.,d:They are exempt from traffic laws.
note: Bicyclists generally have the same rights and duties as motor vehicle drivers and can be cited or ticketed for violating traffic laws.

question: If you have a green light but pedestrians are crossing against their signal, what must you do?
options: a:Honk to make them hurry,b:Speed up and pass in front of them,c:Stop or yield to allow pedestrians to cross safely,d:Proceed without slowing because they are at fault.
note: Drivers must exercise due care to avoid colliding with pedestrians in the roadway, even if the pedestrians are crossing against their signal. You should slow down and stop or yield as necessary to allow them to cross safely, then proceed when the crosswalk is clear.

question: A diamond-shaped sign is used to indicate:
options: a:A school crossing specifically.,b:An interstate route.,c:A speed limit.,d:A road hazard or warning.
note: Diamond-shaped signs are warning signs used to indicate road hazards or changes in roadway conditions ahead.

question: A regulatory sign showing a red circle with a slash through a black symbol means:
options: a:The area is a construction zone.,b:The action shown is prohibited.,c:Some drivers must yield to others.,d:Drivers should stop completely.
note: A red circle with a slash over a black symbol on a regulatory sign indicates that the depicted action is prohibited.

question: What causes 'highway hypnosis' and how can it be prevented?
options: a:Only occurs when driving at high speeds.,b:Frequent rest stops cause it.,c:Staring at the road for long periods reduces active scanning; prevent it by frequently scanning and taking breaks.,d:Sleeping too much the night before leads to it.
note: Highway hypnosis can occur when a driver stares straight ahead at the road for long periods without actively scanning, leading to reduced alertness. It can be prevented by frequently moving your eyes, scanning mirrors and surroundings, and taking regular rest breaks.

question: Where is it illegal to park?
options: a:In a parking lot.,b:On a hill.,c:On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.
note: Parking is unlawful in marked bicycle lanes or on crosswalks. When parking on the street, you must also park parallel and within the required distance of the curb (commonly within 12–18 inches, depending on state law).

question: How should you respond to an aggressive driver on the road?
options: a:Speed up to keep ahead of them.,b:Cut them off to slow them down.,c:Avoid eye contact,d:Retaliate by tailgating them.
note: Remain calm, avoid eye contact and provocative gestures, create distance, and, when safe, allow the aggressive driver to pass or move away from you. Do not engage, race, or retaliate.

question: An inattentive driver is someone who:
options: a:Stares off the roadway or daydreams while driving.,b:Maintains eye contact with a passenger when driving.,c:Only watches the vehicle directly ahead of them.,d:Constantly checks mirrors while driving.
note: An inattentive driver is one whose attention is not properly on the driving task, such as staring off the roadway or daydreaming. This prevents proper scanning and increases crash risk.
