Maintaining prolonged eye contact with a passenger or only watching the vehicle directly ahead can also be forms of inattention, but option a best matches the standard definition.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, how should you turn the steering wheel?
options: a:In the opposite direction of the skid,b:To keep the front wheels straight,c:In the direction you want the vehicle to go
note: If your vehicle begins to skid, take your foot off the accelerator and steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go (in the direction of the skid). As the vehicle begins to straighten out, carefully adjust the steering to keep control.

question: When driving near a motorcycle you must:
options: a:Follow closer than you would other vehicles.,b:Allow the motorcycle to use only half of a lane.,c:Drive on the shoulder beside the motorcycle.,d:Allow the motorcycle to use a full lane.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane width, just like any other motor vehicle. Do not crowd them, share their lane, or drive alongside them in the same lane.

question: If you miss your freeway exit, what is the correct action?
options: a:Pull onto the shoulder and back up to the exit,b:Make a U-turn through the median,c:Continue to the next exit and safely return to your desired route
note: If you pass your exit, do not stop, back up, or turn across lanes. Proceed to the next exit and re-route safely.

question: What should you do when road surfaces become slippery due to rain, snow, or sleet?
options: a:Reduce your speed below the posted limit and drive with extra caution.,b:Drive at the posted speed because limits are safe in all conditions.,c:Increase your following distance only if others do so.,d:Use cruise control to maintain traction.
note: When roads are slippery, slow down below the posted speed if needed and increase your following distance; in many cases the safe speed is below the posted limit.

question: What penalties can you face for providing false information on a DMV application in Oregon?
options: a:Only a small administrative fee.,b:A brief driving quiz only.,c:An immediate lifetime ban from driving.,d:Driver license suspension or cancellation for up to one year and possible criminal charges with fines or imprisonment.
note: In Oregon, knowingly providing false information on a driver license or ID application can result in suspension or cancellation of your driving privileges for up to one year and may be prosecuted as a crime (often a misdemeanor) with possible fines and/or jail time, depending on the specific statute violated and circumstances.

question: When an emergency vehicle using lights and/or siren approaches, what must you do immediately?
options: a:Slow down but remain in your lane.,b:Turn on your four-way flashers only.,c:Accelerate to get ahead of it.,d:Pull to the right and stop as soon as it is safe.
note: When approached by an emergency vehicle using lights and/or siren, you must immediately pull to the right and stop when it is safe, giving it a clear path.

question: At a basic crossbuck railroad crossing with no gates or lights, what should you do?
options: a:Always stop even when no train is visible.,b:Drive faster than the train to beat it across.,c:Turn down your radio to try to hear a train.,d:Approach with extreme caution and cross only when you know no train is near.
note: At a crossbuck railroad crossing without gates or flashing lights, slow down, look and listen carefully, and cross only when you are sure no train is near and it is safe to proceed.

question: Why should you avoid following other cars too closely?
options: a:You may not see the vehicle's turn signals,b:You may not have enough time to stop if the vehicle ahead slows or stops suddenly,c:You may not see the road between the cars
note: Following too closely reduces your margin to react and stop safely if the vehicle ahead brakes suddenly.

question: What color are regulatory signs typically, and what is required of drivers?
options: a:Blue; they are only suggestions.,b:Orange; they indicate temporary rules only.,c:White with black or red markings; they must be obeyed.,d:Green; they are informational only.
note: Regulatory signs are usually white with black or red markings and convey laws or regulations that must be followed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a flashing yellow traffic signal mean?
options: a:Stop and wait for a green light,b:Slow down and proceed with caution,c:Speed up to clear the intersection quickly
note: A flashing yellow means you should slow down, look carefully, and proceed through the intersection with caution when it is safe to do so. Stopping is not required unless needed for safety.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn, to whom must you yield the right-of-way?
options: a:Only to drivers turning right,b:No one—you have the right-of-way,c:Oncoming traffic and any pedestrians or other road users already in the intersection
note: When making a left turn, you must yield to oncoming traffic and to pedestrians and other road users already in or entering the intersection or crosswalk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do when entering a roadway from a private road or driveway?
options: a:Drive out quickly to avoid delaying others.,b:Yield to pedestrians and traffic on the roadway before entering.,c:Stop with part of your car in the roadway to alert drivers.,d:Blow your horn to warn traffic you are entering.
note: When entering a roadway from a private road or driveway, you must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians and to all traffic already on the roadway before entering.

question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, what must drivers do?
options: a:Follow the directions given by the flagger.,b:Follow the vehicle ahead even if the flagger disagrees.,c:Ignore the flagger unless a police officer is present.,d:Continue at the same speed.
note: Flaggers control traffic in work zones; you must obey their signals and directions, as they have the same authority as a traffic control device in construction zones.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do when facing a red traffic signal?
options: a:Stop only if a police officer is present.,b:Proceed if the crosswalk is clear.,c:Slow down and proceed if there is no cross traffic.,d:Stop before entering the intersection.
note: A steady red light means you must come to a complete stop before entering the intersection, at the stop line, or before the crosswalk, and remain stopped until the light turns green or you are otherwise permitted to proceed (such as a permitted right turn on red where allowed and safe).

question: If you feel worried, nervous, angry, or very emotional, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Call someone while driving to calm down.,b:Drive immediately; emotions don't affect ability.,c:Take time to calm down and focus before starting to drive.,d:Drive faster to get to your destination sooner.
note: Strong emotions can distract you and impair your judgment and reaction time. Take time to calm down and regain focus before starting to drive to ensure safety.

question: How can you check blind spots before changing lanes?
options: a:Turn your head and glance over the shoulder in the direction you plan to move.,b:Rely only on the inside rearview mirror.,c:Use the outside mirror only.,d:Use your turn signal without looking.
note: Before changing lanes, briefly turn your head and glance over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to check areas not visible in your mirrors (blind spots).

question: Why should you be cautious when passing a bicyclist?
options: a:Because you are moving faster than the bicycle.,b:Oncoming traffic may not see you pull out to pass.,c:The bicycle always has the right-of-way.
note: You should be cautious when passing a bicyclist because oncoming traffic may not see you pull out to pass and may not expect you to move into their lane. In addition, bicyclists may need to swerve to avoid hazards, so you must give them extra space and pass only when it is safe and legal.

question: A round traffic sign usually warns drivers of:
options: a:A no passing zone.,b:A school zone.,c:An upcoming railroad crossing.,d:An upcoming hospital zone.
note: Round traffic signs are typically used to warn of an upcoming railroad crossing.

question: If you are in an accident and someone is injured, what should you do?
options: a:Move the injured person away from the scene immediately.,b:Avoid moving the injured unnecessarily.,c:Always leave injured people where they are and avoid providing aid.
note: Do not move injured persons unless there is immediate danger (such as fire, explosion risk, or traffic hazard). Avoid moving them unnecessarily; control bleeding if you can, keep them warm, and wait for trained emergency responders.

question: What is the safe way to drive through a curve?
options: a:Maintain a single constant speed throughout the curve.,b:Increase speed as you enter and then brake sharply at the exit.,c:Brake hard throughout the curve to stay slow.,d:Slow down as you enter the curve and accelerate gradually as you exit.
note: Reduce speed before entering a curve and then increase speed smoothly as you exit to maintain control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection of two similar roads, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The vehicle approaching from the left.,b:The fastest vehicle.,c:The vehicle approaching from the right.,d:The vehicle that honks first.
note: At intersections without signs or signals, yield to vehicles approaching from your right.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane, two-way road, what must you do?
options: a:Cross into the oncoming traffic lane only when it is safe and legal.,b:Use the shoulder to pass when necessary.,c:Flash headlights at oncoming traffic to warn them.,d:Pass on the right anytime.
note: On a two-lane, two-way road, you may pass a slower vehicle only by entering the oncoming traffic lane when it is clearly safe and legal to do so, and when passing is not prohibited by signs or pavement markings.

question: Where is it especially important to reduce speed?
options: a:Only on open highways.,b:On narrow or winding roads,c:Only when driving behind a slow-moving vehicle.,d:Only when directed by a policeman.
note: Reduce speed in narrow or winding areas, at intersections, near railroad crossings, on hills and blind curves, and whenever road conditions are poor.

question: When driving through an area where children are playing, you should expect them to:
options: a:Possibly run into the street without looking, so slow down and be ready to stop.,b:Always stop at the curb before crossing.,c:Know when it is safe to cross.,d:Yield to your vehicle.
note: Children may act unpredictably and could run into the road without looking; reduce speed and be prepared to stop.

question: How would you best describe distracted driving?
options: a:Very uncommon.,b:Extremely risky behavior that endangers you and others.,c:A behavior only new drivers engage in.,d:Something of little concern.
note: Distracted driving is extremely risky behavior that diverts your attention from the driving task and dramatically increases crash risk for you, your passengers, and other road users.

question: What should you do when preparing to change lanes?
options: a:Only check the side view mirror,b:Quickly turn your head without checking mirrors first,c:Check side and rearview mirrors and then quickly glance over your shoulder to check the blind spot,d:Check mirrors and blind spot before changing lanes.
note: Before changing lanes, check your rearview and side mirrors to see traffic behind and to the sides, then quickly glance over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to check your blind spot. Change lanes only when it is safe.

question: Which driving habit helps conserve gasoline?
options: a:Revving the engine while parked.,b:Accelerating quickly from stops.,c:Slowing down gradually and anticipating stops and traffic flow.,d:Sitting in your driveway with the engine running.
note: Looking ahead, anticipating stops and traffic flow, and slowing down gradually instead of accelerating hard or idling unnecessarily helps conserve gasoline and improve fuel economy.

question: Which factor affects your ability to stop your vehicle?
options: a:The color of your car.,b:The type of license plate you have.,c:The condition of the road and weather (road surface).,d:The music playing in your car.
note: Stopping ability depends heavily on the condition of the road surface and weather (wet, icy, gravel, etc.); you should reduce speed when conditions are poor.

question: How can you reduce the chance of hydroplaning?
options: a:Drive more quickly to get through wet spots.,b:Drive through shallow water at speed.,c:Drive more slowly.
note: Hydroplaning risk increases with speed on wet roads. To reduce the chance of hydroplaning, slow down on wet pavement and ensure your tires have good tread and are properly inflated.

question: How should you check blind spots before changing lanes to avoid collisions?
options: a:Rely only on your rearview mirror.,b:Honk just before changing lanes.,c:Adjust your exterior mirrors every few minutes.,d:Turn your head and glance over your shoulder in the direction you intend to move.
note: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and then turn your head and glance over your shoulder in the direction you intend to move to check your blind spot; do not rely exclusively on mirrors.

question: Which headlights should you use when driving in dense fog?
options: a:Parking lights only.,b:No lights at all to avoid glare.,c:Low beam headlights (and fog lights if equipped).,d:High beam headlights.
note: In dense fog, use low beam headlights, and fog lights if your vehicle is equipped with them. High beams can reflect off the fog and reduce your visibility.

question: If another driver cuts you off, how should you react?
options: a:Block them from passing.,b:Let it go and avoid escalating the situation.,c:Flash high beams aggressively.,d:Pull up beside them and shout.
note: If another driver cuts you off, stay calm, slow down if needed, and let it go. Do not try to retaliate or escalate the situation, as that can lead to road rage and unsafe driving.

question: Who benefits most from seat belts being worn?
options: a:The driver only.,b:Only passengers on long trips.,c:All occupants of a car — seat belts are most effective when everyone is buckled.
note: Seat belts are most effective when every occupant is restrained; unbelted occupants can become projectiles in a crash and injure themselves and others.

question: Why must you use extra caution near pedestrians carrying a white cane or using a guide dog?
options: a:They are blind, so you must yield and be prepared to stop to avoid injuring them.,b:They are deaf and may not hear you.,c:They are police officers.,d:They always yield to vehicles.
note: A white cane or guide dog indicates a blind or visually impaired pedestrian. You must use extra caution, slow down, yield the right-of-way, and be prepared to stop to protect them.

question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?
options: a:You never need to stop at a crossing unless a train is visible.,b:All crossings are equipped with lights and gates.,c:Not all crossings have flashing signals or gates; do not go around lowered gates and obey flaggers or signs.,d:It is legal to go around lowered gates during light traffic.
note: Not all railroad crossings have flashing signals or gates. Always slow down, look and listen for trains, obey all signs, signals, and flaggers, and never drive around lowered gates.

question: If you're taking a non-prescription medication, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Read the drug label for warnings about driving.,b:Assume it's safe because it's not prescribed.,c:Drink alcohol to counteract side effects.,d:Ignore any warnings and drive normally.
note: Many over-the-counter medications, such as cold or allergy remedies, can make you drowsy or otherwise impair driving. Always read the label for driving warnings and consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are unsure.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching a flashing yellow traffic signal, what should you do?
options: a:Increase speed to clear the area faster.,b:Come to a complete stop every time.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow traffic signal warns of a potential hazard. You must slow down, proceed with caution, and be prepared to yield to other traffic and pedestrians as necessary.

question: When passing a vehicle that has just parked at the curb, what should you assume and do?
options: a:Assume the driver may open a door and use extra caution.,b:Speed up to pass quickly.,c:Slam on your brakes to avoid any sudden movements.
note: When passing parked vehicles, assume occupants may open doors or step out; slow down and pass with extra caution.

question: Which device is commonly used on highways to direct drivers into the proper lanes for turning?
options: a:Lane-use arrows painted on the pavement and signs.,b:White posts on the shoulder.,c:Flashing yellow lights.,d:Flashing red lights.
note: Lane-use arrows painted on the pavement and accompanying signs are commonly used on highways to indicate which lanes are for turning and which are for through traffic, helping drivers move into the proper lane in advance.

question: How should you prepare for potential hazards coming up on the road ahead?
options: a:Stare straight ahead at all times so you don't miss anything.,b:Continuously scan the roadway and roadsides to identify hazards early.,c:Only watch directly in front of the vehicle.,d:Keep your left foot lightly on the brake to react faster.
note: Search and scan the entire roadway and its sides to spot hazards early and increase your ability to respond safely.

question: When must you yield to emergency vehicles?
options: a:Only if an officer directs you to do so.,b:Only when police vehicles have activated lights.,c:Never; they must find their own path.,d:Whenever you see flashing lights or hear a siren
note: You must yield to emergency vehicles using flashing lights or sirens by pulling over and stopping when safe.

question: When dealing with pedestrians, what is the driver's responsibility?
options: a:Do everything possible to avoid striking pedestrians and yield the right-of-way to them.,b:Always expect pedestrians to yield to vehicles.,c:Yield only to pedestrians in marked crosswalks.,d:Only yield if a crossing guard is present.
note: Drivers must be alert to pedestrians and yield the right-of-way to prevent collisions, even if the pedestrian is crossing improperly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must a driver do when approaching a flashing red traffic signal?
options: a:Slow down but do not stop.,b:Stop.,c:Merge to the right and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing red traffic signal means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. Stop before the crosswalk or limit line, yield to other traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From which lane should you begin a left turn on multilane one-way streets or highways?
options: a:The right lane.,b:The left lane.,c:The middle of the intersection.
note: When turning left from a multilane one-way street or highway, start from the leftmost lane and turn into the leftmost lane of the street you enter.

question: How can you help ensure your physical condition doesn't make driving unsafe?
options: a:Drive regardless of how you feel,b:Ignore doctor advice about driving,c:Know how medications affect driving
note: Be aware of how any medical conditions and medications affect your ability to drive. Follow your doctor's advice, avoid driving when impaired by illness, fatigue, or medication side effects, and drive only when it is safe to do so.

question: If an approaching train is close enough to be a danger, you must:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution across the tracks.,b:Rely on other motorists to warn you.,c:Not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.,d:Cross quickly before the train arrives.
note: If a train is close enough to pose a danger, you must not cross the tracks. Wait until the train has completely passed, the warning devices (if any) have stopped operating, and you have checked that it is safe before crossing.

question: When may you park or stop on a freeway shoulder?
options: a:Whenever you turn on four-way flashers.,b:Only in an emergency; otherwise it is prohibited.,c:If you need to read a map.,d:If no part of your car is on the roadway.
note: Parking or stopping on a freeway shoulder is prohibited except in an emergency, such as a breakdown or medical issue. If you must stop, move as far onto the shoulder as possible and use your hazard flashers.

question: When must you stop for a school bus on a two-lane highway?
options: a:If the bus is stopped on the shoulder with no one aboard.,b:Only when students are crossing in front of the bus.,c:Never; buses must yield to traffic.,d:When the school's bus red lights are flashing and it is stopped.
note: On two-lane roads, traffic in both directions must stop when a school bus displays flashing red lights or its stop arm is extended. You must remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.

question: When railroad crossing signals are flashing, what must you do?
options: a:Cross quickly to beat the train.,b:Drive around any lowered gates if no train is visible.,c:Slow down and look both ways before crossing.,d:Stop no closer than 15 feet from the nearest rail when signals indicate an approaching train.
note: If lights are flashing or gates are down, you must stop at a safe distance from the tracks—no closer than 15 feet from the nearest rail—and remain stopped until the signals stop and it is safe to proceed.

question: What do orange-colored traffic signs usually indicate?
options: a:Temporary work zones or construction ahead.,b:Regulatory instructions like speed limits.,c:School zones.,d:Tourist information.
note: Orange signs typically warn drivers of temporary highway work zones or construction areas and usually have black symbols or lettering.

question: When must you stop at a railroad crossing?
options: a:When you feel like it is unsafe to cross.,b:Only if gates are down and red lights are flashing.,c:Only if a train is visible.,d:Only if directed by a flagger.
note: You must stop at a railroad crossing when: a train is clearly visible or is so close as to be an immediate hazard; a stop sign is posted; a flagger directs you to stop; or warning devices such as flashing red lights, bells, or lowered gates indicate an approaching train. You should also stop any time you judge it is unsafe to proceed across the tracks.

question: If another car is about to hit you, how should you warn them?
options: a:Wave your arms out the window.,b:Use your interior lights to signal them.,c:Speed up and drive away.,d:Sound your horn to alert the other driver or pedestrian.
note: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians when you believe they may not see you and a collision could occur.

question: When an emergency vehicle is approaching with lights and siren, you must pull over to the edge of the road and stop:
options: a:Regardless of the emergency vehicle's direction of travel.,b:Only if it is behind you.,c:Only if it is coming toward you from the opposite direction.,d:Only if the vehicle is identified as a police car.
note: You must pull over to the right edge of the road and stop for an emergency vehicle using lights and siren, regardless of whether it approaches from behind or ahead, unless otherwise directed by a police officer. This applies on most standard roadways; on divided highways with a median, you generally are not required to stop for emergency vehicles on the opposite side if there is a physical barrier.

question: On a road with no sidewalks, which side should a pedestrian walk on?
options: a:The side with the lightest traffic.,b:The same side as traffic is moving.,c:The side facing oncoming traffic (toward vehicles).,d:Anywhere convenient without regard to traffic.
note: On roads without sidewalks, pedestrians should walk on the side facing oncoming traffic so they can see approaching vehicles and react if necessary. This usually means walking on the left side of the road, toward traffic.

question: Does the type of alcoholic beverage (beer, wine, spirits) change how alcohol affects your reflexes and judgment?
options: a:Beer impairs less than wine.,b:Hard ciders impair more than other drinks.,c:Wine impairs less than beer.,d:The effect depends on how much alcohol enters the bloodstream.
note: The impairing effect of alcohol depends on how much alcohol you consume, how quickly you drink it, your body size, and how fast your body absorbs it—not on whether it is beer, wine, or spirits. A standard drink of each type contains about the same amount of alcohol and impairs you similarly.

question: May you drive around or under a gate at a railroad crossing that is being lowered or raised?
options: a:Only if a flagger waves you through.,b:No — never go around or under a moving gate.,c:Yes if your vehicle won't damage the gate.,d:Yes if no train is visible.
note: You must never drive around or under a gate at a railroad crossing while it is lowering, down, or rising. Wait until the gates are fully raised and the warning lights and bells have stopped before proceeding, even if you do not see a train.

question: Which kinds of drugs may impair your ability to drive?
options: a:Only illegal drugs.,b:Only over-the-counter cold medicine.,c:Many kinds of drugs, including prescription, over-the-counter, and illegal drugs.
note: Many kinds of drugs can impair your ability to drive safely, including prescription medications, over-the-counter drugs (such as some cold or allergy medicines), and illegal drugs. Always read labels and warnings, and do not drive if a drug may affect your alertness, coordination, or judgment.

question: If you borrow an unfamiliar vehicle, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Start driving immediately because all cars function the same.,b:Only check the horn and headlights.,c:Hide any defects from the owner.,d:Familiarize yourself with the location and operation of signals
note: When driving an unfamiliar vehicle, you should first familiarize yourself with the location and operation of the turn signals, lights, wipers, brakes, gear selector, and horn, and make sure there are no obvious safety defects before driving.

question: If you are in a line of traffic crossing railroad tracks that has no signals or gates, what must you ensure?
options: a:You have the right-of-way and can stop on the tracks.,b:You can stop on the tracks briefly to check for trains.,c:You may pass slower drivers while on the tracks.,d:You have enough room to get completely across the tracks without stopping and should never pass another vehicle as you approach the crossing.
note: When approaching and crossing railroad tracks, you must ensure there is enough room for your vehicle to completely clear the tracks before you enter the crossing. Never stop on the tracks and never pass another vehicle as you approach or drive over the crossing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which traffic signal requires you to stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when clear?
options: a:A solid green light,b:A flashing yellow light,c:A flashing red light
note: A flashing red signal functions like a stop sign: come to a complete stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when it is safe.

question: Which of the following commonly causes traffic accidents?
options: a:Keeping a larger than necessary following distance.,b:Always driving under the speed limit.,c:Driving too fast for conditions,d:Using turn signals too often.
note: Driving too fast for conditions is a common cause of collisions. Drivers must adjust speed to road, traffic, and weather conditions to maintain control and stop safely.

question: What is true about drivers who have consumed alcohol before driving?
options: a:They do not have sufficient control over their bodies, minds, or vehicles,b:They are always more careful,c:They are fully aware of the risks
note: Alcohol impairs judgment, coordination, vision, and reaction time; even small amounts can reduce a driver's control over their body, mind, and vehicle.

question: By driving on Oregon roads, you have implicitly agreed to what regarding DUII testing?
options: a:You consent to take breath, blood, or urine tests if arrested for DUII.,b:You must maintain liability insurance forever.,c:You can refuse testing without consequence.,d:You're required to post bail immediately.
note: Under Oregon’s Implied Consent Law, by driving on public roads you consent to breath, blood, or urine tests if you are lawfully arrested for DUII. Refusal or failure of these tests results in license suspension and other penalties.

question: Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are divided by what color lines?
options: a:Yellow.,b:White.,c:Red.,d:Black.
note: White lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a flashing yellow arrow for left turns mean?
options: a:You should merge immediately without yielding,b:You may turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians,c:You must come to a complete stop before turning
note: A flashing yellow arrow for a left turn means you may turn left, but you must first yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when the way is clear.

question: Stop lines painted across traffic lanes indicate:
options: a:Only where churches and schools are located.,b:The exact location where you must stop at intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.,c:An upcoming stop sign.,d:Where you may idle your vehicle.
note: Stop lines painted across traffic lanes show the exact place where you must stop at an intersection or at a pedestrian crosswalk when required to stop by a sign, signal, or other traffic control.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing without gates or flashing lights, you should:
options: a:Shift gears while crossing to avoid stalling.,b:Cross quickly without looking both ways.,c:Always stop before crossing the tracks.,d:Be prepared to yield to any train and cross only when safe.
note: At a railroad crossing without gates or flashing lights, you must slow down, look and listen for trains, be prepared to yield, and cross only when you are sure it is safe and there is enough room to clear the tracks completely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before making a left turn, what must you do regarding other road users?
options: a:Sound your horn first.,b:Yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.,c:Swing to the right side of your lane.
note: When turning left you must yield the right-of-way to oncoming traffic and to pedestrians in the crosswalk before completing the turn.

question: Which of the following affect how alcohol affects you?
options: a:Only the amount of food in your stomach.,b:All of the above (amount of food in your stomach, body weight, and time between drinks).,c:Only your body weight.,d:Only how much time passes between drinks.
note: Blood alcohol concentration is influenced by several factors, including how much you drink, the time between drinks, your body weight, and how much food is in your stomach. Food can slow alcohol absorption but does not prevent impairment.

question: When changing lanes, what steps must you take?
options: a:Change lanes quickly without signaling to minimize time exposed.,b:Only check your blind spot after moving over.,c:Flash your headlights as your only signal.,d:Signal your intention, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to be sure the lane is clear before changing lanes.
note: When changing lanes, you must signal your intention, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before moving into the new lane.

question: When is it permissible to cross a solid yellow center line?
options: a:At any time.,b:To pass traffic moving in the same direction.,c:Only to make a left turn into or out of a driveway, side road, or to enter/exit the roadway.
note: A solid yellow line separates traffic moving in opposite directions. You may cross a single solid yellow line only to make a left turn into or out of a driveway, side road, or to enter/exit the roadway, but not to pass another vehicle.

question: When are you allowed to cross double solid yellow centerlines?
options: a:To turn left into or from a driveway, side road, or alley, or to make a legal U-turn where permitted.,b:To pass a slow-moving truck.,c:To pass another car.
note: Double solid yellow centerlines mean no passing or lane changes from either direction. However, you may cross them to make a left turn into or from a driveway, side road, or alley, or to make a legal U-turn where permitted.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, who goes first?
options: a:Drivers must make hand motions to communicate.,b:The vehicle on the left has the right-of-way.,c:The vehicle on the right has the right-of-way (the vehicle on the left must yield).
note: When two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. If vehicles do not arrive at the same time, the one that arrives first proceeds first.

question: When backing your vehicle, how should you look to check behind you?
options: a:Turn your head and look through the rear window; do not rely only on mirrors.,b:Rely solely on your mirrors.,c:Open the door to look behind you.
note: When backing, you should turn your head and look directly through the rear window to check behind you. Use mirrors and any sensors or cameras only as supplements, not as your sole method of checking.

question: What is the purpose of highway pavement markings?
options: a:They are usually unimportant,b:They are only used in construction zones,c:They provide important information that helps drivers position vehicles and follow traffic rules
note: Highway pavement markings provide important information to help drivers position their vehicles, identify lanes and passing zones, and follow traffic rules safely.

question: When approaching any railroad crossing, what actions should you take?
options: a:Slow down, look for trains, and be ready to stop; if lights flash or gates are down, stop 15–50 feet before the tracks.,b:Increase speed to clear the crossing quickly.,c:Drive around a lowered gate if you are running late.,d:Stop only if you hear a train.
note: When approaching any railroad crossing, slow down, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop. If warning lights are flashing or gates are down, you must stop between 15 and 50 feet from the nearest rail and never drive around lowered gates.

question: What do pennant-shaped road signs indicate?
options: a:School zones.,b:Hospital nearby.,c:Speed limits.,d:No passing zones.
note: Pennant-shaped signs (a sideways triangle pointing to the right) are used to indicate the beginning of a no passing zone.

question: What shape is a stop sign?
options: a:Rectangle.,b:Square.,c:Circle.,d:Octagon.
note: A stop sign is eight-sided—an octagon—and tells drivers to come to a complete stop before proceeding.

question: How should a seat belt be adjusted?
options: a:Across your neck for better support.,b:Hidden beneath the seat for comfort.,c:Snug across the hip bones and lower abdomen; shoulder belt comfortable across chest.,d:Loose so you can move easily.
note: Lap belts should fit snugly across the hip bones (not the stomach) and the shoulder belt should lie across the center of the chest and over the shoulder, never across the neck or under the arm, for proper protection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway, what is usually best?
options: a:Proceed slowly and wait for an opening.,b:Turn on your hazard lights until safely merged.,c:Stop at the end of the ramp and look both ways.,d:Accelerate on the ramp to match the speed of freeway traffic and merge when safe.
note: Use the acceleration lane to increase your speed to match the flow of freeway traffic and merge when it is safe; vehicles already on the freeway generally have the right-of-way.

question: What should you do first when visibility decreases?
options: a:Reduce your speed.,b:Turn on your windshield wipers only.,c:Turn on interior lights.,d:Turn on headlights high beams.
note: When visibility decreases, your first response should be to reduce your speed so you have more time and distance to see and react to hazards. Then, as appropriate, use proper lights and wipers.

question: When driving in fog, which of the following precautions should you take?
options: a:Maintain highway speed because visibility will improve soon.,b:Turn off headlights to reduce glare.,c:Use high beams to see further ahead.,d:Drive cautiously at reduced speeds
note: Fog reduces visibility, so you should drive cautiously at reduced speeds and use low-beam headlights or fog lights. Do not use high beams in fog because they reflect off the moisture droplets and increase glare.

question: What do crossbuck signs indicate?
options: a:School zone.,b:No passing zone.,c:Railroad crossing ahead.
note: A crossbuck sign marks a railroad crossing; you must yield to trains and never try to outdrive an approaching train.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see a steady yellow traffic signal, what should you do?
options: a:Continue because you have the right-of-way,b:Accelerate to beat the red light,c:Slow to a stop unless you are already in the intersection
note: A steady yellow warns that the light will soon turn red. Stop safely if you can do so; if already in the intersection, clear it.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you enter a freeway from an on-ramp?
options: a:Signal, yield to traffic, and merge at the speed of traffic.,b:Enter slowly; freeway traffic will yield to you.,c:Stop at the ramp and wait for a large gap.,d:Drive on the shoulder until a gap appears.
note: Use the acceleration lane to match freeway speed, signal, and yield to traffic already on the freeway when merging.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection, if you and a vehicle to your right arrive at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:You should force the other vehicle to stop.,b:Right-of-way alternates randomly.,c:You should speed up to get through first.,d:The vehicle on your right has the right-of-way
note: At an uncontrolled intersection where two vehicles arrive simultaneously, yield to the vehicle on your right.

question: When should you increase your following distance?
options: a:When behind a large vehicle that blocks your view, in bad weather, when exiting an expressway, or when following motorcycles or bicycles.,b:Only when following cars that are smaller than yours.,c:You should keep the same following distance at all times.,d:Only at night.
note: Increase following distance in situations that reduce visibility or traction, such as behind large vehicles, bad weather, or when following motorcycles or bicycles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an officer is directing traffic at an intersection with working signals, which do you follow?
options: a:Honk to get the officer's attention.,b:Follow the officer's directions rather than the signal lights.,c:Wait for another officer to confirm.,d:Always follow the traffic signal regardless of the officer.
note: An officer directing traffic overrides traffic signals and signs; follow the officer's instructions.

question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, you must:
options: a:Ignore the guard during busy hours.,b:Follow what other drivers are doing instead of the guard.,c:Assume the guard has no authority to direct traffic.,d:Follow the crossing guard's directions and use extra caution.
note: Obey directions given by a crossing guard in a school zone and be prepared to reduce speed and exercise caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before entering a roundabout, you must yield to:
options: a:No one; you have the right-of-way entering.,b:Pedestrians and all vehicles already in the roundabout.,c:Only motor vehicles in the roundabout.,d:Only pedestrians in the roundabout.
note: Before entering a roundabout, you must yield to pedestrians and bicyclists crossing the approach and to all vehicles already in the roundabout. Drivers entering never have the right-of-way over traffic already circulating.

question: Under Oregon's Implied Consent Law, what have you agreed to by driving in the state?
options: a:To submit to a breath, blood, or urine test if arrested for DUII.,b:To always carry proof of insurance.,c:To appear in court for all traffic stops.,d:To never refuse any traffic officer's request.
note: By driving in Oregon you consent to chemical testing (breath, blood, or urine) if arrested for driving under the influence of intoxicants (DUII).

question: What can happen if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medication?
options: a:The medication will negate the alcohol.,b:The combination may multiply the impairing effects of both the alcohol and the medicine.,c:The alcohol will help the medicine work faster.
note: Mixing alcohol with prescription or over-the-counter medicines can increase or multiply the impairing effects of both, making you more impaired than you might expect from either one alone.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A single dashed yellow line between opposing lanes means:
options: a:Both lanes travel in the same direction.,b:Drivers may pass when it is safe to do so.,c:Passing is allowed only between dawn and dusk.,d:Drivers may not pass under any circumstances.
note: A single dashed yellow centerline between opposing lanes means vehicles traveling in either direction may pass when it is safe and legal to do so.

question: What is the single most effective thing to reduce injury or death in a crash?
options: a:Wear your seat belt.,b:Drive only on weekdays.,c:Always stay in the right lane.,d:Keep windows open.
note: Wearing a seat belt is widely recognized as the single most effective way to reduce the risk of death or serious injury in a crash.

question: Why is a leaky exhaust system dangerous?
options: a:It only increases pollution,b:It can allow carbon monoxide to enter the passenger compartment and cause poisoning,c:It can cause loss of hearing
note: A leaky exhaust system can allow carbon monoxide, a colorless and odorless poisonous gas, to enter the passenger compartment and cause serious illness or death.

question: When a traffic signal shows a steady yellow arrow, what should drivers do?
options: a:Slow and stop if it is safe to do so, because a red arrow is coming.,b:Merge into the lane in the arrow direction.,c:Turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic.
note: A steady yellow arrow means the movement indicated by the arrow is ending and a red arrow is about to appear. Drivers should slow and stop if it is safe to do so, unless they are so close to the intersection that stopping safely is not possible.

question: Motorcycles are entitled to:
options: a:Half the width of a lane.,b:The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.,c:The bicycle lane only.,d:To be followed more closely than other vehicles.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to the same full lane width as any other motor vehicle. Other drivers should not share a lane side-by-side with a motorcycle.

question: What are the colors of signs that indicate distance to the next highway exit?
options: a:Black with white letters.,b:Yellow with black letters.,c:Green with white letters.,d:Red with white letters.
note: Destination and distance signs on highways are green with white lettering.

question: If stranded in a snowstorm, what is the best course of action?
options: a:Lie down in your car and go to sleep,b:Walk onto the highway to flag down cars.,c:Stay with your vehicle and wait for help; you are more likely to be found if you remain with it.,d:Leave the vehicle immediately to walk for help.
note: If stranded in severe winter weather, you should generally stay with your vehicle, conserve fuel and warmth, and wait for help; you are more likely to be found with your vehicle, and walking away can put you at greater risk.

question: May you drive around lowered gates at a railroad crossing when the train has passed?
options: a:When the train has passed.,b:Under no circumstances—never go around lowered gates.,c:When the lights have stopped flashing but the gate is still down.
note: Never drive around or under a lowered railroad crossing gate. You must wait until the gates are fully raised, the lights have stopped flashing, and you have checked that the tracks are clear in both directions before crossing.

question: Signaling before turns or lane changes is:
options: a:Only needed during the maneuver,b:Only necessary if other traffic is present.,c:A required practice and a good driving habit — signal well in advance.,d:Optional in residential areas.
note: You must signal before turning or changing lanes—typically for at least the last 100 feet before the turn (or longer at higher speeds). Signaling well in advance is both legally required and a safe driving habit.

question: A flashing red traffic signal at an intersection requires you to:
options: a:Come to a complete stop and then proceed when it is safe, just like a stop sign.,b:Slow down but you do not need to stop.,c:Yield only if other vehicles are present.,d:Ignore it and proceed normally.
note: A flashing red signal means you must come to a complete stop, yield to pedestrians and other traffic, and then proceed only when it is safe—treat it the same as a stop sign.

question: Your blind spot refers to which area?
options: a:An area you cannot see without moving your head.,b:The area directly behind your vehicle.,c:The area you see in your rearview mirror.,d:The space directly in front of your bumper.
note: Blind spots are areas alongside and slightly behind your vehicle that you cannot see in your mirrors without turning your head. To check them, you must briefly turn your head and look over your shoulder.

question: What is the most common color of general warning signs?
options: a:Green.,b:Yellow.,c:Blue.,d:Red.
note: Most general warning signs in the United States are diamond-shaped and yellow with black symbols or lettering. These signs alert drivers to potential hazards or changes in road conditions ahead.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are stopped in line at a stop sign and the cross-traffic clears after the cars ahead proceed, what must you do?
options: a:Slowly roll past the stop sign without stopping.,b:Proceed without stopping since the way is clear.,c:Stop again at the stop sign or stop line before going.
note: You must come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection each time you reach the stop sign. Even if the vehicles ahead of you have already stopped and gone, you must stop again at the proper stopping point before proceeding when it is safe.

question: Which of the following helps prevent hydroplaning?
options: a:Using cruise control at high speeds in wet weather.,b:Driving with parking lights only.,c:Accelerating through puddles.,d:Keeping tires with good tread and proper inflation and reducing speed in wet conditions.
note: To reduce the chance of hydroplaning, ensure your tires have good tread, are properly inflated, and reduce your speed when roads are wet. Avoid sudden acceleration, hard braking, and using cruise control in heavy rain.

question: Which statement about changing weather and driving is true?
options: a:If weather changes suddenly, you should adjust your driving; slow down in rain or fog and be aware of vehicles behind you.,b:Weather changes rarely affect driving.,c:Increase speed in fog for better visibility.
note: If weather changes suddenly, you must adjust your driving. In rain, fog, snow, or other adverse conditions, slow down, increase your following distance, and be especially aware of vehicles behind and around you, as not all drivers will adjust their speed appropriately.

question: When you see a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, what should you do?
options: a:Take the right-of-way because you are in a vehicle.,b:Speed up to pass quickly.,c:Honk to get their attention.,d:Slow down, yield, and be prepared to stop.
note: When you see a blind pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog, you must slow down, yield the right-of-way, and be prepared to stop. Do not honk, rev your engine, or otherwise startle the person. Blind pedestrians have the legal right-of-way at crossings.

question: As alcohol builds up in your blood, what occurs?
options: a:Your reactions slow and you make more errors while feeling more confident.,b:You become less confident and more cautious.,c:Your body metabolizes alcohol more quickly.
note: Increasing blood alcohol concentration slows your reactions, impairs judgment, and often makes you feel more confident than you should. This combination leads to more driving errors and risky decisions.

question: Which traffic signal indicates you should slow down and proceed with caution through an intersection?
options: a:A flashing red light.,b:A steady green light.,c:A flashing yellow light.,d:A solid yellow light.
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution, yielding as necessary and being prepared to stop if needed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must drivers do when approaching a steady red traffic light?
options: a:Come to a complete stop; right turn on red is allowed unless prohibited by sign.,b:Drive through if no other vehicles are present.,c:Proceed slowly because the light will change soon.,d:Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
note: At a steady red light, you must come to a complete stop before the crosswalk or limit line. After stopping, you may turn right on red unless a sign prohibits it, and only when it is safe and after yielding to pedestrians and other traffic.

question: If other drivers around you are acting angrily, what should you do?
options: a:Don’t make eye contact and avoid gestures.,b:React with hand gestures to show displeasure.,c:Distance yourself from the situation by slowing down or moving over safely.,d:Confront them to resolve the conflict.
note: If other drivers are acting angrily or aggressively, do not make eye contact, do not respond with gestures or confront them, and safely create distance by slowing down, changing lanes, or exiting the roadway when appropriate.

question: What is the best way to handle a driver who is tailgating you?
options: a:Slam on your brakes to scare them off.,b:Stop abruptly to punish them.,c:Speed up to create distance instantly.,d:Gradually slow down or change lanes to encourage them to pass.
note: If another vehicle is following too closely, the safest response is to gradually slow down or, when safe, change lanes so the tailgater can pass. Avoid sudden braking or speeding up, as these can increase the risk of a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection, if two vehicles arrive at the same time, who must yield?
options: a:The largest vehicle has the right-of-way.,b:The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.,c:The car on the left has the right-of-way.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection where two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield the right-of-way to the driver on the right.

question: What should you adjust first when you get into a car to drive?
options: a:Your seat position so you can see and reach controls.,b:Your rearview mirror before adjusting the seat.,c:Your seat belt only, then drive.,d:The steering wheel before setting the seat.
note: You should first adjust your seat so you can comfortably reach the pedals and controls and have good visibility. After the seat is properly adjusted, then adjust your mirrors, steering wheel, and fasten your seat belt.

question: What does a red arrow on a traffic signal mean?
options: a:Proceed slowly through the intersection.,b:Stop then proceed when clear.,c:Stop and remain stopped until the signal changes to a green light or green arrow.
note: A red arrow means you must stop and remain stopped in the direction of the arrow until a green light or green arrow appears, unless a sign specifically allows a turn on red.

question: When parallel parking between two cars, what should you do first?
options: a:Turn your wheels immediately to the left.,b:Back in without aligning first.,c:Pull up even with the car in front of the space,d:Turn your wheels immediately to the right.
note: When parallel parking between two vehicles, you should first pull up so that your car is parallel and even with the car in front of the space, signal, and then begin backing into the space while turning the wheel as appropriate.

question: A driver extending their left arm and hand downward is signaling that they plan to:
options: a:Stop.,b:Turn right.,c:Turn left.
note: A driver extending their left arm and hand downward is using the standard hand signal for slowing or stopping. Left arm straight out indicates a left turn; left arm bent upward indicates a right turn.

question: An octagonal traffic sign always means:
options: a:Speed limit.,b:Railroad crossing.,c:Hospital ahead.,d:Stop.
note: An octagonal (eight-sided) traffic sign is used exclusively for STOP signs in the United States. When you see an octagonal sign, you must come to a complete stop at the appropriate stopping point.

question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, what is the safest response?
options: a:Call the police immediately while continuing to engage with them.,b:Flash your lights and make rude gestures to let them know they're wrong.,c:Speed up and chase them down to confront them.,d:Stay calm and safely move out of the aggressive driver's way.
note: If cut off by an aggressive driver, remain calm and get out of their way. Avoid eye contact, gestures, or any actions that could escalate the situation, and focus on driving safely.

question: Why is it important to maintain a space cushion around your vehicle?
options: a:It prevents distractions from other vehicles.,b:It gives you time to react to unexpected situations and avoid collisions.,c:It keeps traffic flowing faster.,d:It allows you to park more easily on the roadside.
note: Leaving a space cushion around your vehicle provides time and room to react to hazards, sudden stops, or mistakes by other drivers, helping you avoid collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a flashing yellow light at an intersection mean?
options: a:The intersection is closed for repairs.,b:Make a U-turn because it is unsafe.,c:Proceed with caution through the intersection.,d:Stop and wait for the light to change.
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution, yielding as necessary to other traffic and pedestrians.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a double solid yellow centerline indicate?
options: a:Lanes move in opposite directions and drivers are not permitted to pass.,b:Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is permitted when safe.,c:Lanes move in the same direction and passing is prohibited.,d:Only commercial vehicles may pass.
note: Two solid yellow lines mean traffic in both directions is separated and vehicles may not cross the lines to pass, except to make a left turn or U-turn where permitted.

question: If you are involved in an accident, what actions should you take?
options: a:Drive away if damage seems minor.,b:Only exchange insurance information and leave.,c:Stop immediately and remain at the scene, provide aid if safe, exchange information, and report the crash when required.
note: If you are involved in a crash, you must stop immediately at or near the scene, check for injuries, render reasonable aid if it is safe to do so, exchange information with the other parties, and report the crash to law enforcement when required by law. Never leave the scene of a reportable crash.

question: Your vehicle’s stopping distance increases under which condition?
options: a:On wet or icy roads.,b:On paved highways in good weather.,c:When driving at night only.,d:When traveling downhill always decreases stopping distance.
note: Stopping distance increases on wet, icy, snowy, or loose gravel surfaces, and also at higher speeds or when going downhill. Reduce speed and increase following distance in these conditions.

question: Which effects are caused by alcohol?
options: a:Improved reaction time.,b:Loss of concentration.,c:No effects at low amounts.
note: Alcohol impairs judgment, coordination, vision, and concentration even at low levels; it is always risky and illegal to drive when impaired by alcohol.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do before making a turn?
options: a:Turn the wheel immediately.,b:Increase your speed.,c:Signal in advance (about 3–4 seconds).
note: Signal at least 3–4 seconds (or about 100 feet at lower speeds) before turning so other road users know your intentions and can react safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must not drive at a speed that is:
options: a:Above the maximum speed limit only.,b:Faster than is reasonable and prudent for conditions,c:Exactly the speed of surrounding traffic.,d:Below the posted speed limit.
note: Drive at a speed that is reasonable and prudent for current road, weather, traffic, and visibility conditions. Even if you are below the posted maximum speed limit, you can be driving too fast for conditions if circumstances require slower speeds.

question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle approaching, what should you do?
options: a:Drive as far to the right as safely possible and stop until the vehicle passes.,b:Stop immediately in your lane wherever you are.,c:Proceed slowly and try to let it pass on the left.,d:Speed up to get out of its way.
note: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle using its siren and/or flashing lights, you must immediately yield the right-of-way by pulling as far to the right side of the road as safely possible and stopping until the vehicle has passed. Do not stop in the middle of an intersection; clear the intersection first, then pull over and stop.

question: When sharing the road with large trucks, what is important to remember?
options: a:Trucks always stop more quickly than cars.,b:They can always swerve to avoid you easily.,c:Trucks require longer stopping distances than smaller vehicles.,d:Trucks have smaller blind spots than cars.
note: Large trucks are heavier and require a longer distance to stop than smaller vehicles. When driving near trucks, avoid cutting in front of them and allow extra space for them to slow or stop.

question: Which is a common sign of a drunk driver?
options: a:Driving more slowly than traffic all the time,b:Stopping only at stop signs,c:Weaving between lanes
note: Common signs of an impaired or drunk driver include weaving or drifting between lanes, inconsistent speed, sudden or unnecessary braking, and delayed reactions. While driving significantly slower than traffic can also be a sign, weaving between lanes is a classic and more clearly recognized indicator.

question: If it begins to sleet or snow while you are driving, what should you do?
options: a:Keep windows and mirrors clear and allow extra following distance,b:Drive closer than usual to other vehicles,c:Reduce vigilance and rely on ABS
note: If it begins to sleet or snow while you are driving, slow down, keep your windows and mirrors clear, and increase your following distance to allow for longer stopping distances on slippery roads.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a highway from an entrance ramp, what should you normally do?
options: a:Drive on the shoulder until you find a gap.,b:Use the acceleration lane to reach highway speed and merge when safe.,c:Enter slowly and force other vehicles to yield.,d:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait.
note: Acceleration lanes allow you to increase speed to match the flow of traffic on the highway. Use the acceleration lane to reach highway speed, signal, check mirrors and blind spots, yield to traffic already on the highway, and merge when it is safe.

question: When preparing to turn left, what should drivers do?
options: a:Ignore pedestrians since cars have priority.,b:Speed up and move into the right lane.,c:Stop in the middle of the intersection and wait.,d:Signal in advance.
note: When preparing to turn left, you should signal well in advance (typically at least 100 feet or 3–5 seconds before the turn), slow down gradually, move into the proper left lane or left-turn lane when safe, and yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians. You should not stop in the middle of the intersection unless you have entered on green and are waiting for a gap to complete the turn.

question: Which of these does NOT affect blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Time between drinks.,b:Amount consumed.,c:The type of alcoholic beverage (beer, wine, or liquor).,d:Body weight.
note: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is primarily affected by how much alcohol you drink, how quickly you drink it (time between drinks), your body weight, and other physiological factors. The type or brand of alcoholic beverage (beer, wine, or liquor) by itself does not change how your body absorbs alcohol; what matters is the total amount of pure alcohol consumed.

question: If you hit an unattended parked vehicle and cannot find the owner, what must you do?
options: a:Drive away if no one saw you.,b:Wait until the police arrive and do nothing else.,c:Leave a written note with your name, address, contact information, and an explanation of the accident.,d:Only leave a note if the damage is severe.
note: If you hit an unattended parked vehicle and cannot locate the owner, you must stop, try to find the owner, and if you cannot, leave a written note in a conspicuous place on the vehicle with your name, address, contact information, and a brief description of the accident. In many states you must also report the collision to law enforcement, especially if damage exceeds a specified amount.

question: What does flashing amber lights on a school bus indicate?
options: a:The bus is stalled and you should cautiously pass.,b:The bus is preparing to stop to load or unload children — prepare to stop.,c:The bus has finished loading and is leaving.
note: Flashing amber (yellow) lights on a school bus indicate that the bus is preparing to stop to load or unload children. You should slow down and be prepared to stop. When the red lights are flashing and the stop arm is extended, you must stop as required by law.

question: What combination provides the best protection in a crash?
options: a:Only a lap belt,b:Only an airbag,c:A lap-and-shoulder safety belt used with an airbag
note: Belt and airbag together provide the most effective protection; airbags are supplemental and work best when belts are used.

question: What is a 'No zone' in relation to large vehicles?
options: a:A marked no-parking area.,b:The large blind spots around trucks and buses where smaller vehicles disappear from view.,c:A one-way lane for heavy vehicles.,d:A place where passing is always illegal.
note: ‘No zones’ are large blind spots around big vehicles; avoid lingering in them to remain visible to the truck or bus driver.

question: What does a single dashed white line between lanes indicate?
options: a:The lanes move in the same direction and you may change lanes or pass when it is safe.,b:Lanes move in opposite directions.,c:Passing is never allowed.,d:You must stop at the line.
note: A dashed white line separates lanes moving in the same direction and may be crossed when it is safe to change lanes or pass.

question: When parking uphill with a curb, how should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Sharply away from the curb.,b:Slightly to the right.,c:Sharply toward the curb.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn the front wheels sharply away from the curb so that if the vehicle rolls, the back of the front tire will rest against the curb instead of rolling into traffic.

question: Where are roads most likely to freeze first in cold or wet weather?
options: a:On bridges and overpasses.,b:In shaded areas such as sections covered by trees or buildings.,c:At intersections only.,d:On sharp curves only.
note: Bridges, overpasses, and other elevated roadways tend to freeze before the rest of the road because cold air surrounds them from above and below. Shaded areas can also stay icy longer than open areas, so use extra caution in both locations.

question: Drowsy drivers may:
options: a:Stay alert by opening a window and turning up the radio.,b:Drive so poorly that they may appear to be intoxicated.,c:Drink coffee to become fully alert indefinitely.,d:Drive better on long straight roads.
note: Drowsiness can severely impair driving performance and may resemble the impairment caused by alcohol.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you see a steady green arrow on a traffic signal, what does it mean?
options: a:You may turn in the arrow's direction after yielding to traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection.,b:You must stop completely before turning.,c:You should merge into the lane indicated without yielding.
note: A steady green arrow means you are permitted to proceed only in the direction of the arrow. This is a protected movement: oncoming traffic and conflicting traffic are stopped by a red light. You must still yield to any vehicles or pedestrians already in the intersection and to pedestrians lawfully in the crosswalk.

question: If your vehicle begins to slide on a slippery road, what should you do first?
options: a:Firmly apply your brakes.,b:Take your foot off the gas pedal.,c:Apply your parking brake.
note: If your vehicle begins to slide on a slippery road, the first thing you should do is take your foot off the gas pedal to allow the vehicle to slow down gradually. Avoid slamming on the brakes; if you need to slow further, brake gently and steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go.

question: Does drinking coffee after alcohol reduce your blood alcohol concentration?
options: a:Yes — it cancels the alcohol's effects.,b:Only if you drink a lot of coffee.,c:No — coffee does not lower your BAC.,d:Yes — it immediately decreases your BAC.
note: Caffeine may make you feel more alert but it does not reduce blood alcohol concentration or sober you up.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: The space you need to cross traffic safely depends on which factors?
options: a:Road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.,b:The presence of a stop sign only.,c:How loudly you honk your horn.,d:Time of day only.
note: The gap you need to cross traffic safely depends on road and weather conditions and on the speed and distance of oncoming traffic.

question: If you experience a tire blowout while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Take your foot off the gas, do not brake immediately, gradually slow down, and steer to a safe spot to stop.,b:Immediately slam on the brakes.,c:Immediately accelerate to stabilize the vehicle.,d:Turn off the ignition while moving.
note: On a blowout, ease off the accelerator, keep a firm grip on the steering wheel, avoid sudden braking, allow the vehicle to slow gradually, signal, and steer to a safe place off the road before stopping.

question: What is the act of looking over your shoulder to check a blind spot before changing lanes called?
options: a:Unnecessary if you have mirrors.,b:A bad driving habit.,c:A good driving habit (checking your blind spot).,d:An unsafe maneuver.
note: Turning your head to quickly look over your shoulder to check your blind spot before changing lanes or merging is a good driving habit and is required in addition to using your mirrors.

question: How should you respond when an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing lights?
options: a:Pull over to the side and stop, yielding the right-of-way.,b:Keep driving but try to stay out of its way.,c:See if you can reach your destination first.,d:Speed up and move away only if it is behind you.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing lights and/or siren, you must yield the right-of-way by pulling to the right side of the road and stopping where safe. If you are in an intersection, clear the intersection first, then pull over and stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What action is required at an intersection with a flashing red light?
options: a:Slow down and proceed without stopping.,b:Stop only if other cars approach.,c:Stop completely.,d:Ignore the light if you are in a hurry.
note: A flashing red light is treated the same as a stop sign: you must come to a complete stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe to do so.

question: When it begins to rain while you are driving, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down and increase your following distance.,b:Drive faster than surrounding traffic.,c:Turn on four-way flashers and continue at the same speed.,d:Maintain the maximum posted speed.
note: When it begins to rain, especially during the first few minutes, the road can become very slippery. You should slow down, increase your following distance, and turn on your low-beam headlights. If visibility or traction becomes too poor, pull over safely and wait for conditions to improve.

question: If your accelerator sticks while driving, what is the recommended procedure?
options: a:Reach down and try to pull the pedal up,b:Shift into park while moving,c:Shift to neutral
note: Keep control of the vehicle, shift to neutral, brake steadily, steer to a safe area, then turn off the ignition once you are safely stopped. Do not turn the ignition to the lock position while moving, and do not reach down to pull up the pedal while the vehicle is in gear.

question: When must you stop for a pedestrian at an intersection?
options: a:Only if in a marked crosswalk.,b:Only if the pedestrian is directly in front of your car.,c:When the pedestrian is in either a marked or unmarked crosswalk.
note: Drivers must yield and, when necessary, stop for pedestrians in both marked and unmarked crosswalks at intersections. Always give pedestrians the right-of-way when they are in the crosswalk or close enough to be in danger.

question: When parking uphill next to a curb, what should you do with your steering?
options: a:Keep the front tires straight ahead.,b:Turn your front wheels away from the curb.,c:Keep the rear tires against the curb.
note: When parking uphill next to a curb, set the parking brake and turn your front wheels away from the curb. If the vehicle rolls, the front of the tire will contact the curb and help stop the vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a steady green light at an intersection permit you to do?
options: a:Drive faster to clear the intersection quickly.,b:Always turn left without yielding.,c:Stop and wait for a pedestrian to wave you through.,d:Proceed through the intersection if the way is clear and yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection.
note: A steady green light means you may proceed straight or turn (unless a sign prohibits the turn) if the way is clear. You must yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to vehicles already in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which is a good general rule to remember about passing?
options: a:Pass on the right whenever possible.,b:Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only when necessary and legal.,c:Continuously pass slow vehicles to get to the front of traffic.,d:Always exceed the posted speed limit when passing.
note: A good general rule is to drive with the flow of traffic, obey the speed limit, and pass only when it is legal, necessary, and safe. Passing should not be continuous or done by exceeding the speed limit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are driving so slowly that traffic is backing up behind you on a two-lane, two-way road, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up suddenly to match the flow of traffic.,b:Pull off the right side of the road at a safe place and let the traffic pass.,c:Stop in the lane until traffic clears.,d:Maintain your slow speed and refuse to let others pass.
note: When you are impeding traffic by driving unusually slowly on a two-lane, two-way road, you should pull off the road at a safe place and allow other vehicles to pass when it is safe to do so.

question: Which of the following describes how alcohol affects you?
options: a:It slows reaction time, gives false confidence, and impairs thinking and judgment.,b:It improves coordination.,c:It enhances night vision.
note: Alcohol impairs inhibition, judgment, coordination, and reaction time; it can give a false sense of confidence while reducing driving ability.

question: What are dangers of worn or bald tires?
options: a:They increase stopping distance.,b:They make turning more difficult.,c:They raise the risk of hydroplaning.,d:All of the above.
note: Worn or bald tires increase stopping distance, reduce traction (making turning and control more difficult), and raise the risk of hydroplaning. All of the listed effects are dangers of worn tires.

question: When should you slow down while exiting a highway?
options: a:Only when you see toll booths.,b:On the main road just before the exit lane.,c:After you have moved into the exit lane.
note: You should not slow down abruptly while still in the main travel lanes. First move safely into the exit lane, then reduce your speed to the posted ramp or exit speed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a turn you must usually do what to your speed?
options: a:Increase your speed to clear the intersection.,b:Vary the speed unpredictably.,c:Reduce your speed to maintain control during the turn.,d:Keep accelerating until the turn is complete.
note: Before and during most turns, you should reduce your speed to a safe level so you can maintain control, stay in your lane, and respond to hazards.

question: If your accelerator becomes stuck, what should you do first?
options: a:Blow your horn and signal other drivers,b:Slam on the brakes immediately,c:Shift into neutral
note: If the accelerator sticks, stay focused, shift to neutral first, then brake steadily while steering to a safe area. Once safely off the road, turn off the engine carefully.

question: If you hear a siren behind you, what is the proper response?
options: a:Stop immediately where you are even in the travel lane.,b:Speed up to get out of the way quickly.,c:Pull over to the right and stop to let the emergency vehicle pass.,d:Turn into the opposite lane to create space.
note: When an emergency vehicle using sirens and/or flashing lights approaches from behind, safely pull over to the right edge of the road and stop until it has passed, unless otherwise directed by law enforcement.

question: What should the driver of a small vehicle be prepared for when passing a large truck?
options: a:Reduced pollution behind the truck.,b:Wind gusts that can push a smaller vehicle off course.,c:Loud passenger announcements.,d:That the truck will slow to let you pass.
note: When passing a large truck, be prepared for strong wind gusts and air turbulence that can affect your steering and push a smaller vehicle off course. Hold the wheel firmly and pass safely and promptly.

question: When roads are wet, what should drivers remember?
options: a:Roads are especially slippery just after rain begins,b:All of the above,c:Hydroplaning is possible
note: When roads are wet, you should remember that roads are especially slippery just after the rain begins, hydroplaning is possible at higher speeds, and you must give yourself more stopping distance than usual. All of these are true, so the correct choice is the option that includes all of the above.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it illegal to drive slower than the posted speed limit?
options: a:Only when driving in rural areas.,b:When driving so slowly that you disrupt the normal flow of traffic.,c:When someone is following too closely behind you.,d:When in heavy traffic in a construction zone.
note: It is illegal in many situations to drive so slowly that you impede or disrupt the normal flow of traffic, unless reduced speed is necessary for safety or required by law. In such cases, you may be required to pull over to let traffic pass.

question: Why does driving at night require increased caution?
options: a:Because traffic moves faster at night.,b:Because there are always more vehicles at night.,c:Because drivers cannot see as well in the dark and must use headlights between half an hour after sunset and half an hour before sunrise.,d:Because headlights are not allowed on highways.
note: Reduced visibility at night limits a driver's ability to see hazards; headlights are required during specified low-light periods (commonly from half an hour after sunset to half an hour before sunrise, and any time visibility is poor).

question: When another vehicle approaches you at night from the opposite direction, which headlight setting should you use?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:Use fog lights only.,d:Turn off headlights and use parking lights.
note: Do not use high beams when approaching or following another vehicle at night; use low beams to avoid blinding other drivers.

question: How does alcohol affect your driving skills and judgment?
options: a:It improves driving skills but harms judgment.,b:It impairs both driving skills and judgment.,c:It only affects judgment at high doses.,d:It has no effect on driving skills or judgment.
note: Alcohol impairs both driving skills and judgment. It negatively affects vision, reaction time, coordination, and decision-making, increasing the risk of crashes even at relatively low blood alcohol levels.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you cross a single broken white or yellow centerline?
options: a:Never under any circumstances.,b:Only when turning left into a driveway.,c:Only during daylight hours.,d:When it is safe to pass or change lanes and you won't interfere with traffic.
