note: A single broken white line separates lanes moving in the same direction and permits lane changes when safe. A single broken yellow centerline separates opposing directions of traffic and permits passing when it is safe and legal, and when you will not interfere with oncoming traffic.

question: Approaching a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, what must you do?
options: a:Keep going at the same speed in your lane.,b:Change lanes away from the stopped vehicle if possible; otherwise slow down and pass carefully.,c:Stop in the travel lane and wait.,d:Drive to the right and stop immediately even if on the freeway.
note: If an emergency vehicle is stopped with lights flashing, most states' 'Move Over' laws require you to move over a lane away from the vehicle if it is safe to do so; if you cannot change lanes safely, you must slow down significantly and pass with extra caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do at an intersection with a flashing red light?
options: a:Come to a full stop, then proceed when safe,b:Slow and pass through without stopping,c:Wait for a flashing green light
note: A flashing red light has the same meaning as a stop sign: you must come to a complete stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe.

question: What steps should you take when changing lanes?
options: a:Signal and change lanes immediately,b:Check mirrors, signal, and check your blind spot before changing lanes,c:Signal
note: When changing lanes, you must signal, check your rearview and side mirrors, and glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Change lanes only when it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should drivers behave when approaching an intersection with a steady green light?
options: a:Stop and check for oncoming traffic before proceeding.,b:Ignore pedestrians crossing the street.,c:Proceed if the intersection is clear but yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection; be prepared to stop if the light changes.,d:Treat it like a four-way stop.
note: A steady green light means you may proceed if the intersection is clear, but you must yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection and be prepared to stop if the light changes or if necessary for safety.

question: How should you drive through turns on slick roads?
options: a:Accelerate quickly while turning.,b:Change lanes quickly to maintain speed.,c:Take turns more slowly than usual to avoid skidding.,d:Brake hard mid-turn if you feel sliding.
note: On slick or slippery roads, you should slow down before the turn and drive through the turn more slowly than usual to reduce the risk of skidding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which has priority: a steady red light, a stop sign, or instructions from a traffic officer?
options: a:The steady red light.,b:The traffic officer's directions.,c:The stop sign.,d:All are equal; follow the most restrictive.
note: Instructions from an authorized traffic officer always take precedence over traffic signals, signs, and pavement markings. You must follow the officer’s directions even if they conflict with the light or sign.

question: An orange-colored sign most commonly means:
options: a:The start of a no passing zone.,b:Construction,c:A school zone is ahead.,d:A recreation area.
note: Orange signs are used to warn drivers of construction, maintenance, or emergency operations in or near the roadway.

question: Defensive driving is best described as:
options: a:Following the car in front of you very closely to block others.,b:Only driving when traffic is light.,c:Getting ahead of other drivers to reduce risk.,d:Identifying dangerous driving situations early and taking action to avoid accidents.
note: Defensive driving means anticipating hazards and taking proactive steps to prevent conflicts and collisions.

question: What are the typical colors of warning signs that indicate upcoming hazards?
options: a:Black on white backgrounds.,b:Green on white backgrounds.,c:Black symbols or letters on a yellow background (work zones are orange).,d:White on blue backgrounds.
note: Warning signs generally use black symbols or lettering on a yellow background to indicate upcoming hazards. Work zone warning signs are orange with black markings.

question: A solid white edge line on the right that angles toward the center of the road indicates:
options: a:A parking area ahead.,b:You must turn left soon.,c:The road ahead becomes narrower.,d:An intersection ahead.
note: If the right edge line slants or angles toward the center of the road, it warns that the road ahead will be narrower, so drivers should be prepared for reduced lane width.

question: When you hear or see an approaching emergency vehicle using lights or siren, what is required?
options: a:Slow down until it passes,b:Drive to the right side of the road and stop until it passes,c:Motion for the emergency vehicle to pass you
note: You must yield to emergency vehicles by pulling to the right and stopping; if you are in an intersection, continue through it, then pull over to the right and stop until the emergency vehicle has passed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you reach an intersection where you want to turn but are not in the proper lane, what should you do?
options: a:Quickly cut across traffic to make the turn.,b:Turn from your current lane after signaling at the last second.,c:Drive to the next intersection and make the turn from the correct lane.,d:Back up into the correct lane.
note: Do not make last-minute turns. Continue to the next intersection and make the turn from the proper lane to avoid dangerous maneuvers.

question: When you see a railroad crossing warning sign, you should:
options: a:Ignore it if no lights are flashing.,b:Speed up to cross before the train arrives.,c:Look for a way around any lowered gates.,d:Be prepared to stop if a train is nearby.
note: Warning signs mean a train may be approaching; be ready to stop, slow down, look and listen for trains, and obey all gates and signals.

question: What is a good way to relieve fatigue on a long trip?
options: a:Drive with one eye closed occasionally to rest the other.,b:Do arm exercises every hour instead of stopping.,c:Stop and rest every two hours or take a short nap if you become drowsy.,d:Drink energy drinks and keep driving.
note: Take regular breaks—about every two hours—and stop to rest or take a short nap if you become drowsy to reduce crash risk from fatigue.

question: Which headlight setting should you use when driving in fog?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Parking lights.,c:Low beam headlights.
note: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow; high beams can reflect off moisture in the air and reduce your visibility.

question: What is the effect of combining drugs with alcohol?
options: a:It is no more dangerous than alcohol alone.,b:It increases the risk of causing a crash.,c:It lessens alcohol's effects on driving ability.
note: Mixing alcohol with any drugs (prescription, over-the-counter, or illegal) increases impairment and greatly increases the risk of causing a crash.

question: You are in the left lane and want to move right. What checks should you make before changing lanes?
options: a:Check mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder for other vehicles.,b:Check mirrors only and then move.,c:Signal and rely only on side mirrors.,d:Look over your left shoulder and move quickly.
note: When changing lanes to the right, you should check your mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder to check your blind spot before moving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When driving on an interstate, what must you do before changing lanes or passing?
options: a:Always use cruise control.,b:Honk and then change lanes immediately.,c:Stop on the shoulder first.,d:Signal, check your mirrors, and check your blind spot before changing lanes or passing.
note: Before changing lanes or passing on an interstate, you must signal, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Only stop on the shoulder in an emergency.

question: Signs that advise drivers of potentially hazardous conditions are called:
options: a:Regulatory signs.,b:Warning signs.,c:Guide signs.,d:Informational signs.
note: Warning signs alert drivers to potentially hazardous conditions ahead; they are often yellow with black symbols or lettering.

question: On average, about how much alcohol does the body eliminate per hour?
options: a:Three alcoholic drinks per hour.,b:About one standard drink per hour.,c:Two drinks per hour.,d:Half a drink per hour.
note: The average person metabolizes roughly one standard alcoholic drink per hour, though many factors such as weight, sex, and food intake affect impairment.

question: If your tire blows out while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Keep driving at the same speed until you reach a service station.,b:Turn on your hazard lights and accelerate to the shoulder.,c:Hold the steering wheel firmly, ease off the accelerator, and steer to a safe place off the road before braking.,d:Slam on the brakes immediately.
note: If your tire blows out, hold the steering wheel firmly, keep the vehicle going straight, ease off the accelerator to slow down gradually, and then carefully steer to a safe place off the road before braking and stopping.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a green arrow changes to a solid green, what must you do when turning?
options: a:You keep the same right-of-way to turn without yielding,b:You may still turn but must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians,c:You may no longer turn and must go straight
note: When a green arrow becomes a solid green, the protected turn ends and you must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians before turning.

question: What should you know about large trucks when driving near them?
options: a:They can stop more quickly than passenger vehicles.,b:They need less room to maneuver than passenger vehicles.,c:They have large blind spots and need more room to stop and maneuver.
note: Large trucks have significant blind spots and require more distance to stop and maneuver due to their size and weight.

question: While driving on major highways, what should you do to avoid 'highway hypnosis'?
options: a:Keep cruise control on at all times.,b:Close one eye occasionally.,c:Stare at a single point on the roadway.,d:Keep your eyes moving and stay alert to be ready for hazards.
note: Staying alert and moving your eyes prevents inattention and helps you react to hazards on long highway trips.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, which vehicle may proceed first?
options: a:The vehicle that arrived last.,b:Only the vehicle on the left.,c:The vehicle that arrived first.
note: At four-way stops, the first vehicle to arrive should proceed first. If two arrive simultaneously, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way.

question: Which of these helps prevent crashes by communicating with other road users?
options: a:Driving only on side streets to avoid traffic.,b:Speeding to get out of others' way.,c:Signaling your intentions and using your horn or emergency signals when appropriate.,d:Ignoring other drivers on the road.
note: Communicating—using turn signals, brake lights, horns, and emergency flashers—helps other road users anticipate your actions and reduces crashes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Who must yield when entering public traffic from a driveway or private road?
options: a:The driver entering from the driveway or private road must yield to traffic already on the public road.,b:The public road traffic must always yield.,c:Neither must yield; proceed cautiously together.,d:Only yield if turning left.
note: Vehicles entering from driveways or private roads must yield to vehicles and pedestrians already on the public roadway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: An arrow painted on the pavement within a traffic lane indicates:
options: a:Drivers in that lane must follow the movement indicated by the arrow (for example, turn only).,b:Drivers may choose to ignore the arrow if they are in a hurry.,c:Drivers must always come to a complete stop before following the arrow.,d:The lane is exclusive for buses only.
note: Pavement arrows indicate the required movements from that lane—drivers must follow the direction shown if they are in that lane.

question: If a pedestrian begins crossing in front of you, how should you respond?
options: a:Slow down and be prepared to stop, yielding the right-of-way if they are in the crosswalk.,b:Flash your headlights to hurry them.,c:Speed up and pass in front of them.
note: Always yield to pedestrians crossing in or entering a crosswalk; reduce speed and stop if necessary to allow them to cross safely. If a pedestrian begins crossing in front of you anywhere on the roadway, slow down and be prepared to stop to avoid endangering them, even if they are not in a marked crosswalk.

question: Which factors affect braking distance?
options: a:Vehicle speed, condition of brakes and tires, and pavement condition (All of the above),b:Only the driver's skill,c:Only the vehicle's color
note: Braking distance depends primarily on vehicle speed, condition of the brakes and tires, and the road surface (including weather-related conditions). Driver perception and reaction time affect total stopping distance, but not the braking distance once the brakes are applied.

question: When must you use your turn signals?
options: a:Only when merging onto a freeway.,b:When changing lanes.,c:Only during night driving.,d:Only when other traffic is present.
note: Turn signals must be used whenever you turn, change lanes, enter or leave a freeway, or pull away from or toward a curb—any time you make a lateral or turning movement that could affect other road users. They are required by law, not only when merging onto a freeway, at night, or only when other traffic is present.

question: If there is an oncoming car to your left and a bicyclist to your right, what should you do?
options: a: Split the difference and squeeze between both hazards., b: Pull onto the shoulder between them., c: Let the oncoming car pass first, d: Pass the bicyclist first quickly and then deal with the oncoming car.
note: When faced with more than one hazard, you should avoid dealing with both at the same time. Slow down and let the oncoming car pass first, then move over safely to pass the bicyclist when there is enough space and it is safe to do so.

question: A ''No stopping'' sign means you may stop only to what action?
options: a: Unload packages at any time, b: Discharge passengers whenever needed, c: Avoid a conflict with other traffic (such as to prevent a crash)
note: A "No Stopping" sign means you may not stop, stand, or park on that portion of the roadway except as necessary to obey a traffic control device or officer, or to avoid conflict with other traffic (such as to prevent a crash). You may not stop there to load/unload passengers or packages.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you not do when changing lanes?
options: a: Use a turn signal to indicate your intentions., b: Check for drivers who might also be moving into the same lane., c: Fail to check side and rearview mirrors.
note: When changing lanes, you must check your side and rearview mirrors, check your blind spot, and use your turn signal to indicate your intentions. You should not fail to check your mirrors before changing lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you not pass another vehicle?
options: a: If the car ahead is signaling to turn right., b: When a bus is stopped on the opposite side of a divided highway., c: On a hill or curve, d: When traveling below the speed limit.
note: You must not pass when your view ahead is blocked, such as on a hill or curve, or in other designated no-passing zones (e.g., near intersections, railroad crossings, and on narrow bridges). Passing is generally allowed if the vehicle ahead is turning right and it is otherwise safe and legal, and a stopped bus on the opposite side of a divided highway usually does not prohibit passing. Traveling below the speed limit alone does not make passing illegal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a street from a driveway, what must you do?
options: a: Stop before the sidewalk and proceed only when no vehicles or pedestrians are approaching., b: Drive slowly to allow others time to get out of the way., c: Honk your horn to warn pedestrians and drivers.
note: When entering a street from a driveway, alley, or private road, you must stop before crossing the sidewalk, yield to pedestrians and all approaching vehicles, and proceed only when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means:
options: a:Do not pass from your direction.,b:Slow down.,c:Pass with caution.
note: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means passing is prohibited from your direction. You must not cross this line to pass another vehicle.

question: For drivers age 21 or older, it is illegal to drive with a minimum blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:
options: a:0.10 percent.,b:0.02 percent.,c:0.08 percent.,d:0.05 percent.
note: For drivers age 21 or older in most US jurisdictions, it is illegal to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.08 percent or higher.

question: If you miss your exit on an expressway, what should you do?
options: a:Signal to the driver beside you for directions,b:Get off at the next exit and return safely to the route you intended,c:Stop and make a U-turn at the median
note: Do not stop, back up, or make a U-turn on an expressway. If you miss your exit, continue to the next exit, leave the expressway, and then return safely to your intended route.

question: If your wheels leave the pavement and drop onto the shoulder, what is the correct action to return safely?
options: a:Speed up and swerve back onto the road quickly.,b:Jerk the steering wheel to force the vehicle back onto the pavement.,c:Reduce speed by gently braking,d:Slam on the brakes immediately.
note: If your wheels leave the pavement and drop onto the shoulder, stay calm, hold the steering wheel firmly, and gradually reduce speed by easing off the accelerator and gently braking if needed. Once you have slowed to a safe speed and the vehicle is under control, carefully steer back onto the pavement. Avoid sudden swerving or jerking the wheel.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic light changes from green to solid yellow as you approach an intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Treat it like a caution sign and continue through at the same speed.,b:Stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely; if not, proceed carefully through.,c:Stop immediately even if it may cause a rear-end collision.,d:Accelerate to beat the red light.
note: A solid yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. You must stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are too close to stop safely when the light turns yellow, proceed carefully through the intersection.

question: Approximately how far might a fully loaded tractor-trailer need to stop when traveling at 55 mph?
options: a:Less than a car's stopping distance.,b:Around 125 feet.,c:About 50 feet.,d:Up to 400 feet.
note: Large trucks take much longer to stop than cars; a fully loaded tractor-trailer at 55 mph may require almost 400 feet to stop under ideal conditions.

question: If a tire blows out while driving, what is the best immediate action?
options: a:Maintain speed and keep steering as before.,b:Turn sharply onto the shoulder.,c:Hold the wheel firmly, steer straight, and ease off the gas.,d:Brake hard immediately to stop quickly.
note: If a tire blows out, firmly hold the steering wheel, keep the vehicle going straight, ease off the accelerator, and let the vehicle slow down gradually. Do not brake hard. Once the vehicle is under control and speed has decreased, carefully steer to the side of the road and stop in a safe place.

question: If your vehicle skids, what is the correct steering response?
options: a:Steer in the direction of the skid (turn into the skid).,b:Overcorrect the wheel to regain control.,c:Turn the wheel away from the direction of the skid.,d:Brake hard immediately.
note: If your vehicle begins to skid, stay calm, take your foot off the accelerator, and steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go (the same direction the rear of the vehicle is sliding) until you regain traction.

question: What is the best way to avoid hydroplaning on wet roads?
options: a:Reduce speed when roads are wet and keep tires properly maintained.,b:Use cruise control to maintain speed.,c:Drive faster to push water aside.,d:Turn sharply to avoid puddles.
note: To reduce the risk of hydroplaning, slow down when roads are wet, avoid sudden maneuvers, keep your tires properly inflated and with good tread, and avoid driving through standing water when possible.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two drivers arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on the right.,b:The driver on the left.,c:The driver in the largest vehicle.,d:The driver who signals first.
note: When two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. The vehicle on the right has the right-of-way.

question: If a fire engine is following you on a two-lane street but is not using emergency signals, what should you do?
options: a:Pull over and stop immediately,b:Speed up to get out of its way,c:Continue driving normally
note: If the emergency vehicle is not displaying lights or using a siren, it is not operating in emergency mode and you are not required to yield. Continue driving normally and obey all traffic laws.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If turning onto a street with multiple lanes going your way, which lane should you enter?
options: a:The lane marked for bicycles.,b:The lane you feel like using at the moment.,c:The far-right lane always.,d:The lane closest to the lane you came from.
note: When turning onto a street with multiple lanes going your way, you must turn into the lane closest to the one you came from, and then change lanes later if needed when it is safe.

question: If you discover a vehicle defect that may affect safety, when should it be repaired?
options: a:Correct the defect as soon as possible before driving.,b:Fix it only when convenient.,c:Drive at slower speeds indefinitely.,d:Ignore it if the vehicle still moves.
note: Any defect that may affect the safe operation of your vehicle should be corrected as soon as possible and before driving. Driving with known safety defects is unsafe and may be illegal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before passing another vehicle, what checks should you make?
options: a:Turn off your headlights.,b:Re-enter your lane within 10 feet of the passed vehicle.,c:Honk at least three times before passing.,d:Check mirrors and blind spots and signal before changing lanes.
note: Before passing, check your mirrors and blind spots, signal your intention, and move into the passing lane only when it is safe. Return to your original lane only after you can safely do so without cutting off the passed vehicle.

question: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder, what should you do?
options: a:Brake hard and sharply steer back onto the road.,b:Stop your car on the edge of the road and re-enter when clear.,c:Slow down and carefully steer back onto the pavement when safe.
note: If your wheels drop off the pavement, ease off the accelerator, slow down, keep a firm grip on the steering wheel, and carefully steer back onto the pavement when traffic and road conditions make it safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you cross a dashed white line?
options: a:Only during daylight hours.,b:At any time regardless of conditions.,c:When it is safe to change lanes or pass.
note: Broken (dashed) white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. You may cross them to change lanes or pass only when it is safe to do so.

question: Which statement about work zones is true?
options: a:Work zones may be moving or stationary and require extra attention.,b:They are always marked with black and white signs.,c:You can drive normally and ignore them.,d:They only occur during daytime.
note: Work zones can be moving (such as mowing or striping operations) or stationary and are usually marked by orange signs. Drivers must slow down, be alert, and use extra caution in these areas.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What do speed limit signs tell drivers?
options: a:Potential driving speeds for the area,b:The maximum or minimum legal speed for the road under ideal conditions,c:The speed to use in heavy traffic
note: Speed limit signs indicate the maximum (or sometimes minimum) lawful speed under ideal conditions. Drivers must reduce speed below the posted limit when road, traffic, or weather conditions make it unsafe to travel at the posted speed.

question: Which is NOT an effect of drinking alcohol?
options: a:Your reflexes and reaction time speed up.,b:You are less alert.,c:Your judgement of speed and distance becomes distorted.
note: Alcohol slows reflexes and reaction time, makes you less alert, and distorts your judgment of speed and distance. It does not speed up your reflexes or improve reaction time.

question: What does a steady yellow traffic light at an intersection indicate you should do?
options: a:Yield to other cars and continue at the same speed.,b:Slow down and prepare to stop because the red light is coming.,c:Go.
note: A steady yellow traffic light warns that the signal is about to turn red. You should slow down and stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely.

question: What actions help prevent rear-end collisions?
options: a: Before stopping, look well ahead and begin slowing early.,b: Release the gas and immediately slam the brakes.,c: Avoid sudden stops whenever possible by slowing gradually and signaling early.
note: To reduce rear-end collisions, avoid sudden stops whenever possible. Look well ahead, ease off the gas early, and apply your brakes gradually so drivers behind you have time to react. Always signal in advance before slowing or stopping.

question: How should you approach railroad tracks when driving?
options: a: Look and listen, slow down, and be prepared to stop,b: Speed up to cross before a gate lowers,c: Try to drive around a lowered gate
note: Always look and listen for trains, slow down, and be prepared to stop. Obey all warning signs, signals, and gates, and never drive around lowered gates or ignore warning devices.

question: In a vertical traffic light arrangement, what is the top-to-bottom order of colors?
options: a: Yellow at the top, red in the middle, green at the bottom,b: Green at the top, yellow in the middle, red at the bottom,c: Red at the top, green in the middle, yellow at the bottom,d: Red at the top, yellow in the middle, green at the bottom
note: In a vertical traffic signal, the standard order from top to bottom is: red at the top, yellow in the middle, and green at the bottom.

question: If someone is driving aggressively behind you, what should you do?
options: a: Try to get out of their way and avoid engaging with them.,b: Stare at them as they pass to show displeasure.,c: Speed up to challenge them.,d: Brake-check them to teach a lesson.
note: If someone is driving aggressively behind you, stay calm, avoid eye contact or gestures, and safely move out of their way when possible. Do not speed up, brake-check, or otherwise engage with them.

question: What can occur if alcohol is combined with another drug?
options: a: Nothing will happen,b: The effects of alcohol and the drug may both be increased,c: The effects may be reduced
note: When alcohol is combined with many other drugs (including some prescription and over-the-counter medications), the effects of both substances can be increased or become unpredictable, greatly increasing impairment and crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection with a yield sign, what should you do?
options: a:Always stop regardless of traffic.,b:Yield the right-of-way to traffic and pedestrians in the intersection or roadway you are entering.,c:Yield only to traffic on your left.,d:Ignore it if no other cars are visible.
note: A yield sign means you must slow down and be prepared to stop if necessary, yielding the right-of-way to traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection or roadway you are entering.

question: Hydroplaning usually occurs from what driving action?
options: a:Driving too fast for wet conditions, reducing tire contact with the road.,b:Frequent stopping.,c:Sudden turns.
note: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast for wet conditions and your tires ride up on a thin layer of water, reducing or losing contact with the road and causing loss of traction and control.

question: To reduce headlight glare from oncoming vehicles at night, where should you look?
options: a:Over your shoulder.,b:Straight at the oncoming lights.,c:Toward the right side of the road ahead.
note: To reduce headlight glare from oncoming vehicles at night, briefly glance toward the right side of the road and use the right edge or lane line as a guide, rather than looking directly at the oncoming headlights.

question: What do work zone signs generally indicate?
options: a:Less-than-ideal driving conditions ahead — slow down and use caution.,b:It is summer and roads are busier.,c:You must immediately stop and back up.,d:Roads are closed only at night.
note: Work zone (orange) signs warn of roadwork and changing or less-than-ideal driving conditions ahead. You should slow down, use caution, and follow any posted directions or flagger instructions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Two solid yellow lines on the pavement mean:
options: a:Only left turns are permitted across the lines.,b:Passing is not allowed from either direction.,c:Passing is allowed at the top of hills only.,d:Passing is allowed for drivers from both directions.
note: Two solid yellow lines in the center of the road mean passing is prohibited for traffic traveling in either direction. You may cross the lines only when making a left turn into or from a driveway, side road, or alley where it is otherwise permitted and safe.

question: When must you yield to a stopped transit bus that is signaling to re-enter traffic?
options: a:Only if there are vehicles directly behind you.,b:Only if the bus turns on its hazard lights.,c:When the bus has its turn signal and activated flashing 'Yield' sign, you must allow it to re-enter by slowing or moving over (where required by state law).
note: In some states, when a transit bus is stopped at a designated stop and is signaling to re-enter traffic with its left turn signal and an activated flashing 'Yield' sign, drivers are required to yield by slowing down or changing lanes to allow the bus to merge safely. However, this is not a universal rule in all U.S. states; it is state-specific. The question and explanation should clarify that this requirement applies where state law mandates yielding to buses displaying a flashing yield sign.

question: When should you signal while preparing to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Early enough to alert other drivers of your intentions before you begin to pass.,b:Only as you start to change lanes.,c:After you have completed the pass.,d:Only if another car is beside you.
note: Signal well in advance of a lane change or pass so others have time to react to your intended maneuver.

question: Which device is most strongly associated with increased crash risk when used by a driver?
options: a:Radio,b:Cell phone (including hands-free),c:CD player,d:Map book
note: Cell phone use (including hands-free) is strongly associated with increased crash risk because it causes cognitive distraction and often visual and manual distraction as well. While radios, CD players, and map books can also distract drivers, research consistently shows that cell phone use is more strongly linked to crash risk than these other devices.

question: Drivers must yield to pedestrians:
options: a:Only at intersections with signals.,b:Only when pedestrians use marked crosswalks.,c:Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the street as the driver.,d:Even if the pedestrian is crossing carelessly.
note: Drivers must exercise due care to avoid colliding with pedestrians and should yield to pedestrians already in the roadway, even if the pedestrian is crossing carelessly or outside a crosswalk. However, this does not give pedestrians the right to suddenly leave a curb or other place of safety and walk or run into the path of a vehicle that is so close it is impossible for the driver to yield. The key point is that drivers must do everything reasonably possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian, regardless of the pedestrian’s carelessness.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You arrive at a 4-way stop at the same time as a driver on your left. Who has the right of way?
options: a:The driver on your left, because they were there first,b:You have the right of way — the driver to your left must yield to you,c:Whoever signals first proceeds first,d:The driver going straight always has priority
note: At a 4-way stop when two vehicles arrive simultaneously, the driver to the RIGHT has the right of way. Since the other driver is to your LEFT, you are to their right — meaning you have the right of way and should proceed first.

question: If you must make an emergency stop on an interstate, what should you do?
options: a:Get out of your vehicle and flag down the first vehicle that passes.,b:Pull off the road, turn on your emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle, if you can.,c:Sound your horn at passing cars to get their attention.
note: If you must stop on an interstate, pull completely off the travel lanes onto the shoulder if possible, turn on your emergency flashers so others can see you, and stay inside your vehicle with your seat belt fastened unless there is an immediate danger such as fire or traffic striking your vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to pass on a two-lane road, what should be your primary check?
options: a:Judge the distance and speed of oncoming vehicles.,b:Flash your headlights as you pass.,c:Sound your horn as you pass.,d:Assume oncoming traffic will slow down.
note: Before passing on a two-lane road, your main concern is whether there is enough clear space ahead in the oncoming lane. Carefully judge the distance and speed of oncoming vehicles and only begin passing if you are sure you can complete the maneuver and return to your lane without forcing any other driver to slow or swerve.

question: On which road marking may you legally pass another vehicle?
options: a:You are on a road with a solid line next to your lane.,b:You are on a hill or curve.,c:You are on a road with a broken line next to your lane.
note: A broken center line next to your lane means you may pass when it is safe. A solid line next to your lane means you must not pass, and you should never pass on hills, curves, or anywhere your view of oncoming traffic is limited.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle, you should move back into your original lane when:
options: a:You have cleared the front bumper of the passed vehicle.,b:You can see the passed vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror.,c:You are 50 feet ahead of the passed vehicle.,d:The passing vehicle signals you to move over.
note: After passing, do not move back into your original lane until you can see the front of the vehicle you passed (its headlights in the daytime or at night) in your rearview mirror. This ensures you have enough space ahead and do not cut off the other driver.

question: What do blue traffic signs generally indicate?
options: a:Regulatory requirements like speed limits.,b:Mileage distances to locations.,c:Construction and maintenance warnings.,d:Information on motorist services (rest areas, hospitals, food).
note: Blue traffic signs are service signs. They give information about motorist services such as rest areas, gas stations, food, lodging, and hospitals along the roadway.
